problem_description.description: The leader of some very secretive organization has decided to invite all other members to a meeting. All members of the organization live in the same town which can be represented as $$$n$$$ crossroads connected by $$$m$$$ two-directional streets. The meeting will be held in the leader's house near the crossroad $$$1$$$. There are $$$k$$$ members of the organization invited to the meeting; $$$i$$$-th of them lives near the crossroad $$$a_i$$$. All members of the organization receive the message about the meeting at the same moment and start moving to the location where the meeting is held. In the beginning of each minute each person is located at some crossroad. He or she can either wait a minute at this crossroad, or spend a minute to walk from the current crossroad along some street to another crossroad (obviously, it is possible to start walking along the street only if it begins or ends at the current crossroad). In the beginning of the first minute each person is at the crossroad where he or she lives. As soon as a person reaches the crossroad number $$$1$$$, he or she immediately comes to the leader's house and attends the meeting.Obviously, the leader wants all other members of the organization to come up as early as possible. But, since the organization is very secretive, the leader does not want to attract much attention. Let's denote the discontent of the leader as follows  initially the discontent is $$$0$$$;  whenever a person reaches the crossroad number $$$1$$$, the discontent of the leader increases by $$$c \cdot x$$$, where $$$c$$$ is some fixed constant, and $$$x$$$ is the number of minutes it took the person to reach the crossroad number $$$1$$$;  whenever $$$x$$$ members of the organization walk along the same street at the same moment in the same direction, $$$dx^2$$$ is added to the discontent, where $$$d$$$ is some fixed constant. This is not cumulative: for example, if two persons are walking along the same street in the same direction at the same moment, then $$$4d$$$ is added to the discontent, not $$$5d$$$. Before sending a message about the meeting, the leader can tell each member of the organization which path they should choose and where they should wait. Help the leader to establish a plan for every member of the organization so they all reach the crossroad $$$1$$$, and the discontent is minimized.
problem_description.input_spec: The first line of the input contains five integer numbers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$, $$$k$$$, $$$c$$$ and $$$d$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 50$$$, $$$n - 1 \le m \le 50$$$, $$$1 \le k, c, d \le 50$$$) — the number of crossroads, the number of streets, the number of persons invited to the meeting and the constants affecting the discontent, respectively. The second line contains $$$k$$$ numbers $$$a_1$$$, $$$a_2$$$, ..., $$$a_k$$$ ($$$2 \le a_i \le n$$$) — the crossroads where the members of the organization live. Then $$$m$$$ lines follow, each denoting a bidirectional street. Each line contains two integers $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$ ($$$1 \le x_i, y_i \le n$$$, $$$x_i \ne y_i$$$) denoting a street connecting crossroads $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$. There may be multiple streets connecting the same pair of crossroads. It is guaranteed that every crossroad can be reached from every other crossroad using the given streets.
problem_description.output_spec: Print one integer: the minimum discontent of the leader after everyone reaches crossroad $$$1$$$.
problem_description.notes: NoteThe best course of action in the first test is the following:  the first person goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the second person waits one minute on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the third person waits two minutes on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the fourth person waits three minutes on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting.

problem_description.description: The leader of some very secretive organization has decided to invite all other members to a meeting. All members of the organization live in the same town which can be represented as $$$n$$$ crossroads connected by $$$m$$$ two-directional streets. The meeting will be held in the leader's house near the crossroad $$$1$$$. There are $$$k$$$ members of the organization invited to the meeting; $$$i$$$-th of them lives near the crossroad $$$a_i$$$. All members of the organization receive the message about the meeting at the same moment and start moving to the location where the meeting is held. In the beginning of each minute each person is located at some crossroad. He or she can either wait a minute at this crossroad, or spend a minute to walk from the current crossroad along some street to another crossroad (obviously, it is possible to start walking along the street only if it begins or ends at the current crossroad). In the beginning of the first minute each person is at the crossroad where he or she lives. As soon as a person reaches the crossroad number $$$1$$$, he or she immediately comes to the leader's house and attends the meeting.Obviously, the leader wants all other members of the organization to come up as early as possible. But, since the organization is very secretive, the leader does not want to attract much attention. Let's denote the discontent of the leader as follows  initially the discontent is $$$0$$$;  whenever a person reaches the crossroad number $$$1$$$, the discontent of the leader increases by $$$c \cdot x$$$, where $$$c$$$ is some fixed constant, and $$$x$$$ is the number of minutes it took the person to reach the crossroad number $$$1$$$;  whenever $$$x$$$ members of the organization walk along the same street at the same moment in the same direction, $$$dx^2$$$ is added to the discontent, where $$$d$$$ is some fixed constant. This is not cumulative: for example, if two persons are walking along the same street in the same direction at the same moment, then $$$4d$$$ is added to the discontent, not $$$5d$$$. Before sending a message about the meeting, the leader can tell each member of the organization which path they should choose and where they should wait. Help the leader to establish a plan for every member of the organization so they all reach the crossroad $$$1$$$, and the discontent is minimized.
problem_description.input_spec: The first line of the input contains five integer numbers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$, $$$k$$$, $$$c$$$ and $$$d$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 50$$$, $$$n - 1 \le m \le 50$$$, $$$1 \le k, c, d \le 50$$$) — the number of crossroads, the number of streets, the number of persons invited to the meeting and the constants affecting the discontent, respectively. The second line contains $$$k$$$ numbers $$$a_1$$$, $$$a_2$$$, ..., $$$a_k$$$ ($$$2 \le a_i \le n$$$) — the crossroads where the members of the organization live. Then $$$m$$$ lines follow, each denoting a bidirectional street. Each line contains two integers $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$ ($$$1 \le x_i, y_i \le n$$$, $$$x_i \ne y_i$$$) denoting a street connecting crossroads $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$. There may be multiple streets connecting the same pair of crossroads. It is guaranteed that every crossroad can be reached from every other crossroad using the given streets.
problem_description.output_spec: Print one integer: the minimum discontent of the leader after everyone reaches crossroad $$$1$$$.
problem_description.notes: NoteThe best course of action in the first test is the following:  the first person goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the second person waits one minute on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the third person waits two minutes on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the fourth person waits three minutes on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting.

problem_description.description: The leader of some very secretive organization has decided to invite all other members to a meeting. All members of the organization live in the same town which can be represented as $$$n$$$ crossroads connected by $$$m$$$ two-directional streets. The meeting will be held in the leader's house near the crossroad $$$1$$$. There are $$$k$$$ members of the organization invited to the meeting; $$$i$$$-th of them lives near the crossroad $$$a_i$$$. All members of the organization receive the message about the meeting at the same moment and start moving to the location where the meeting is held. In the beginning of each minute each person is located at some crossroad. He or she can either wait a minute at this crossroad, or spend a minute to walk from the current crossroad along some street to another crossroad (obviously, it is possible to start walking along the street only if it begins or ends at the current crossroad). In the beginning of the first minute each person is at the crossroad where he or she lives. As soon as a person reaches the crossroad number $$$1$$$, he or she immediately comes to the leader's house and attends the meeting.Obviously, the leader wants all other members of the organization to come up as early as possible. But, since the organization is very secretive, the leader does not want to attract much attention. Let's denote the discontent of the leader as follows  initially the discontent is $$$0$$$;  whenever a person reaches the crossroad number $$$1$$$, the discontent of the leader increases by $$$c \cdot x$$$, where $$$c$$$ is some fixed constant, and $$$x$$$ is the number of minutes it took the person to reach the crossroad number $$$1$$$;  whenever $$$x$$$ members of the organization walk along the same street at the same moment in the same direction, $$$dx^2$$$ is added to the discontent, where $$$d$$$ is some fixed constant. This is not cumulative: for example, if two persons are walking along the same street in the same direction at the same moment, then $$$4d$$$ is added to the discontent, not $$$5d$$$. Before sending a message about the meeting, the leader can tell each member of the organization which path they should choose and where they should wait. Help the leader to establish a plan for every member of the organization so they all reach the crossroad $$$1$$$, and the discontent is minimized.
problem_description.input_spec: The first line of the input contains five integer numbers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$, $$$k$$$, $$$c$$$ and $$$d$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 50$$$, $$$n - 1 \le m \le 50$$$, $$$1 \le k, c, d \le 50$$$) — the number of crossroads, the number of streets, the number of persons invited to the meeting and the constants affecting the discontent, respectively. The second line contains $$$k$$$ numbers $$$a_1$$$, $$$a_2$$$, ..., $$$a_k$$$ ($$$2 \le a_i \le n$$$) — the crossroads where the members of the organization live. Then $$$m$$$ lines follow, each denoting a bidirectional street. Each line contains two integers $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$ ($$$1 \le x_i, y_i \le n$$$, $$$x_i \ne y_i$$$) denoting a street connecting crossroads $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$. There may be multiple streets connecting the same pair of crossroads. It is guaranteed that every crossroad can be reached from every other crossroad using the given streets.

import sys
from collections import deque

def main():
    input = sys.stdin.read
    data = input().split()
    
    idx = 0
    n = int(data[idx]); idx += 1
    m = int(data[idx]); idx += 1
    k = int(data[idx]); idx += 1
    c = int(data[idx]); idx += 1
    d = int(data[idx]); idx += 1
    
    MAX_NODES = 14043
    linkList = []
    adjacency = [[] for _ in range(MAX_NODES)]
    
    totalCost = 0
    INFINITY_VAL = 10**18
    
    sourceVertex = MAX_NODES - 2
    targetVertex = MAX_NODES - 1
    
    def getResidual(link_idx):
        return linkList[link_idx].capacity - linkList[link_idx].flow
    
    def addConnection(u, v, cap, cst):
        adjacency[u].append(len(linkList))
        linkList.append({'endpoint': v, 'capacity': cap, 'flow': 0, 'cost': cst})
        adjacency[v].append(len(linkList))
        linkList.append({'endpoint': u, 'capacity': 0, 'flow': 0, 'cost': -cst})
    
    for i in range(k):
        x = int(data[idx]); idx += 1
        addConnection(sourceVertex, x, 1, 0)
    
    MAX_T = 101
    for t in range(MAX_T):
        addConnection(1 + t * n, targetVertex, k, t * c)
    
    for i in range(m):
        x = int(data[idx]); idx += 1
        y = int(data[idx]); idx += 1
        for t in range(MAX_T - 1):
            for j in range(k):
                cost = d * (2 * j + 1)
                addConnection(x + t * n, y + t * n + n, 1, cost)
                addConnection(y + t * n, x + t * n + n, 1, cost)
    
    for i in range(n):
        for t in range(MAX_T - 1):
            addConnection(i + t * n, i + t * n + n, k, 0)
    
    def findShortestPath():
        distance = [INFINITY_VAL] * MAX_NODES
        parentVertex = [-1] * MAX_NODES
        parentLink = [-1] * MAX_NODES
        inQueue = [False] * MAX_NODES
        
        distance[sourceVertex] = 0
        q = deque()
        q.append(sourceVertex)
        inQueue[sourceVertex] = True
        
        while q:
            u = q.popleft()
            inQueue[u] = False
            
            for link_idx in adjacency[u]:
                if getResidual(link_idx) == 0:
                    continue
                v = linkList[link_idx]['endpoint']
                w = linkList[link_idx]['cost']
                if distance[v] > distance[u] + w:
                    distance[v] = distance[u] + w
                    parentVertex[v] = u
                    parentLink[v] = link_idx
                    if not inQueue[v]:
                        inQueue[v] = True
                        q.append(v)
        
        return distance, parentVertex, parentLink
    
    def updateFlowAlongPath(distance, parentVertex, parentLink):
        nonlocal totalCost
        cur = targetVertex
        while cur != sourceVertex:
            idx = parentLink[cur]
            linkList[idx]['flow'] += 1
            linkList[idx ^ 1]['flow'] -= 1
            cur = parentVertex[cur]
        if distance[targetVertex] != INFINITY_VAL:
            totalCost += distance[targetVertex]
    
    for i in range(k):
        distance, parentVertex, parentLink = findShortestPath()
        updateFlowAlongPath(distance, parentVertex, parentLink)
    
    print(totalCost)

    main()

import heapq
import sys

class MincostFlow:
    class Edge:
        __slots__ = ('v', 'c', 'w', 'r')
        def __init__(self, v, c, w, r):
            self.v = v
            self.c = c
            self.w = w
            self.r = r

    def __init__(self, n):
        self.G = [[] for _ in range(n)]

    def add(self, u, v, c, w):
        i = len(self.G[u])
        j = len(self.G[v])
        self.G[u].append(self.Edge(v, c, w, j))
        self.G[v].append(self.Edge(u, 0, -w, i))

    def run(self, s, t, f):
        N = len(self.G)
        res = 0
        H = [0] * N
        INF = 10**18
        
        while f > 0:
            D = [INF] * N
            D[s] = 0
            PV = [-1] * N
            PE = [-1] * N
            q = [(0, s)]
            
            while q:
                d, u = heapq.heappop(q)
                d = -d
                if D[u] < d:
                    continue
                for i, e in enumerate(self.G[u]):
                    if e.c > 0 and D[e.v] > D[u] + e.w + H[u] - H[e.v]:
                        D[e.v] = D[u] + e.w + H[u] - H[e.v]
                        heapq.heappush(q, (-D[e.v], e.v))
                        PV[e.v] = u
                        PE[e.v] = i
            
            if D[t] == INF:
                return -1
            
            for i in range(N):
                H[i] += D[i]
            
            d = f
            i = t
            while i != s:
                d = min(d, self.G[PV[i]][PE[i]].c)
                i = PV[i]
            
            f -= d
            res += d * H[t]
            
            i = t
            while i != s:
                e = self.G[PV[i]][PE[i]]
                e.c -= d
                self.G[i][e.r].c += d
                i = PV[i]
        
        return res

def main():
    input = sys.stdin.read
    data = input().split()
    
    idx = 0

    A = []
    for i in range(K):
        A.append(int(data[idx]) - 1)
        idx += 1
    
    us = []
    vs = []
    for i in range(M):
        u = int(data[idx]) - 1
        v = int(data[idx+1]) - 1
        idx += 2
        us.append(u)
        vs.append(v)
    
    mcf = MincostFlow(N * 101 + 2)
    s = N * 101
    t = s + 1
    
    for i in range(K):
        mcf.add(s, A[i], 1, 0)

        for j in range(N):

            for k in range(1, K + 1):
                mcf.add(N * i + us[j], N * (i + 1) + vs[j], 1, (2 * k - 1) * D)

    print(mcf.run(s, t, K))

class MCF:
    class Edge:
        __slots__ = ('to', 'cap', 'cost', 'rev')

            self.to = to
            self.cap = cap
            self.cost = cost
            self.rev = rev

    def __init__(self, nodes):
        self.n = nodes
        self.graph = [[] for _ in range(nodes)]

    def add_edge(self, from_node, to_node, capacity, cost):
        rev_to = len(self.graph[to_node])
        rev_from = len(self.graph[from_node])
        self.graph[from_node].append(self.Edge(to_node, capacity, cost, rev_to))
        self.graph[to_node].append(self.Edge(from_node, 0, -cost, rev_from))

    def solve(self, source, sink, flow_needed):
        INF = 10**18
        dist = [INF] * self.n
        potential = [0] * self.n
        prev_node = [-1] * self.n
        prev_edge = [-1] * self.n
        
        total_cost = 0
        while flow_needed > 0:
            dist = [INF] * self.n
            dist[source] = 0
            pq = [(0, source)]
            
            while pq:
                d, u = heapq.heappop(pq)
                if d > dist[u]:
                    continue
                for i, e in enumerate(self.graph[u]):
                    if e.cap > 0 and dist[e.to] > dist[u] + e.cost + potential[u] - potential[e.to]:
                        dist[e.to] = dist[u] + e.cost + potential[u] - potential[e.to]
                        prev_node[e.to] = u
                        prev_edge[e.to] = i
                        heapq.heappush(pq, (dist[e.to], e.to))
            
            if dist[sink] == INF:
                return -1
            
            for i in range(self.n):
                potential[i] += dist[i]
            
            flow = flow_needed
            v = sink
            while v != source:
                u = prev_node[v]
                edge_idx = prev_edge[v]
                flow = min(flow, self.graph[u][edge_idx].cap)
                v = u
            
            flow_needed -= flow
            total_cost += flow * potential[sink]
            
            v = sink
            while v != source:
                u = prev_node[v]
                edge_idx = prev_edge[v]
                e = self.graph[u][edge_idx]
                e.cap -= flow
                self.graph[v][e.rev].cap += flow
                v = u
        
        return total_cost

class FlowEdge:

        self.dest = dest
        self.capacity = capacity
        self.weight = weight
        self.reverse_index = reverse_index

class MinCostFlow:
    def __init__(self, n):
        self.num_nodes = n
        self.adj = [[] for _ in range(n)]
    
    def connect(self, src, dst, cap, wgt):
        reverse_idx_dst = len(self.adj[dst])
        reverse_idx_src = len(self.adj[src])
        self.adj[src].append(FlowEdge(dst, cap, wgt, reverse_idx_dst))
        self.adj[dst].append(FlowEdge(src, 0, -wgt, reverse_idx_src))
    
    def compute(self, source, sink, required_flow):
        dist = [float('inf')] * self.num_nodes
        potential = [0] * self.num_nodes
        parent_node = [-1] * self.num_nodes
        parent_edge = [-1] * self.num_nodes
        
        total = 0
        
        while required_flow > 0:
            dist = [float('inf')] * self.num_nodes
            heap = []
            dist[source] = 0
            heapq.heappush(heap, (0, source))
            
            while heap:
                d, u = heapq.heappop(heap)
                if d != dist[u]:
                    continue
                for idx in range(len(self.adj[u])):
                    e = self.adj[u][idx]
                    if e.capacity > 0 and dist[e.dest] > dist[u] + e.weight + potential[u] - potential[e.dest]:

                        parent_node[e.dest] = u
                        parent_edge[e.dest] = idx
                        heapq.heappush(heap, (dist[e.dest], e.dest))

            node = sink

                e = self.adj[parent_node[node]][parent_edge[node]]
                e.capacity -= flow
                reverse_edge = self.adj[node][e.reverse_index]
                reverse_edge.capacity += flow
                node = parent_node[node]

    def __init__(self, n):
        self.node_count = n

    def add_edge(self, from_node, to_node, capacity, weight):
        idx_from = len(self.graph[from_node])
        idx_to = len(self.graph[to_node])
        self.graph[from_node].append(Edge(to_node, capacity, weight, idx_to))
        self.graph[to_node].append(Edge(from_node, 0, -weight, idx_from))
    
    def compute(self, source, sink, required_flow):
        INF = float('inf')
        distance = [INF] * self.node_count
        potential = [0] * self.node_count
        previous_node = [-1] * self.node_count
        previous_edge_index = [-1] * self.node_count
        
        total_cost = 0
        
        while required_flow > 0:
            distance = [INF] * self.node_count
            pq = []
            distance[source] = 0
            heapq.heappush(pq, (0, source))
            
            while pq:
                d, u = heapq.heappop(pq)
                if d != distance[u]:
                    continue
                for idx in range(len(self.graph[u])):
                    e = self.graph[u][idx]
                    if e.cap > 0 and distance[e.to] > distance[u] + e.cost + potential[u] - potential[e.to]:
                        distance[e.to] = distance[u] + e.cost + potential[u] - potential[e.to]
                        previous_node[e.to] = u
                        previous_edge_index[e.to] = idx
                        heapq.heappush(pq, (distance[e.to], e.to))
            
            if distance[sink] == INF:
                return -1
            
            for i in range(self.node_count):
                potential[i] += distance[i]
            
            flow = required_flow
            v = sink
            while v != source:
                flow = min(flow, self.graph[previous_node[v]][previous_edge_index[v]].cap)
                v = previous_node[v]
            
            required_flow -= flow
            total_cost += flow * potential[sink]
            
            v = sink
            while v != source:
                e = self.graph[previous_node[v]][previous_edge_index[v]]
                e.cap -= flow
                self.graph[v][e.rev].cap += flow
                v = previous_node[v]
        
        return total_cost

All members of the organization live in the same town which can be represented as $$$n$$$ crossroads connected by $$$m$$$ two-directional streets. The meeting will be held in the leader's house near the crossroad $$$1$$$. There are $$$k$$$ members of the organization invited to the meeting; $$$i$$$-th of them lives near the crossroad $$$a_i$$$. All members of the organization receive the message about the meeting at the same moment and start moving to the location where the meeting is held. In the beginning of each minute each person is located at some crossroad. He or she can either wait a minute at this crossroad, or spend a minute to walk from the current crossroad along some street to another crossroad (obviously, it is possible to start walking along the street only if it begins or ends at the current crossroad). In the beginning of the first minute each person is at the crossroad where he or she lives. As soon as a person reaches the crossroad number $$$1$$$, he or she immediately comes to the leader's house and attends the meeting.Obviously, the leader wants all other members of the organization to come up as early as possible. But, since the organization is very secretive, the leader does not want to attract much attention. Let's denote the discontent of the leader as follows  initially the discontent is $$$0$$$;  whenever a person reaches the crossroad number $$$1$$$, the discontent of the leader increases by $$$c \cdot x$$$, where $$$c$$$ is some fixed constant, and $$$x$$$ is the number of minutes it took the person to reach the crossroad number $$$1$$$;  whenever $$$x$$$ members of the organization walk along the same street at the same moment in the same direction, $$$dx^2$$$ is added to the discontent, where $$$d$$$ is some fixed constant. This is not cumulative: for example, if two persons are walking along the same street in the same direction at the same moment, then $$$4d$$$ is added to the discontent, not $$$5d$$$. Before sending a message about the meeting, the leader can tell each member of the organization which path they should choose and where they should wait. Help the leader to establish a plan for every member of the organization so they all reach the crossroad $$$1$$$, and the discontent is minimized.
problem_description.input_spec: The first line of the input contains five integer numbers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$, $$$k$$$, $$$c$$$ and $$$d$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 50$$$, $$$n - 1 \le m \le 50$$$, $$$1 \le k, c, d \le 50$$$) — the number of crossroads, the number of streets, the number of persons invited to the meeting and the constants affecting the discontent, respectively. The second line contains $$$k$$$ numbers $$$a_1$$$, $$$a_2$$$, ..., $$$a_k$$$ ($$$2 \le a_i \le n$$$) — the crossroads where the members of the organization live. Then $$$m$$$ lines follow, each denoting a bidirectional street. Each line contains two integers $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$ ($$$1 \le x_i, y_i \le n$$$, $$$x_i \ne y_i$$$) denoting a street connecting crossroads $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$. There may be multiple streets connecting the same pair of crossroads. It is guaranteed that every crossroad can be reached from every other crossroad using the given streets.
problem_description.output_spec: Print one integer: the minimum discontent of the leader after everyone reaches crossroad $$$1$$$.
problem_description.notes: NoteThe best course of action in the first test is the following:  the first person goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the second person waits one minute on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the third person waits two minutes on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the fourth person waits three minutes on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting.

problem_description.description: The leader of some very secretive organization has decided to invite all other members to a meeting. All members of the organization live in the same town which can be represented as $$$n$$$ crossroads connected by $$$m$$$ two-directional streets. The meeting will be held in the leader's house near the crossroad $$$1$$$. There are $$$k$$$ members of the organization invited to the meeting; $$$i$$$-th of them lives near the crossroad $$$a_i$$$. All members of the organization receive the message about the meeting at the same moment and start moving to the location where the meeting is held. In the beginning of each minute each person is located at some crossroad. He or she can either wait a minute at this crossroad, or spend a minute to walk from the current crossroad along some street to another crossroad (obviously, it is possible to start walking along the street only if it begins or ends at the current crossroad). In the beginning of the first minute each person is at the crossroad where he or she lives. As soon as a person reaches the crossroad number $$$1$$$, he or she immediately comes to the leader's house and attends the meeting.Obviously, the leader wants all other members of the organization to come up as early as possible. But, since the organization is very secretive, the leader does not want to attract much attention. Let's denote the discontent of the leader as follows  initially the discontent is $$$0$$$;  whenever a person reaches the crossroad number $$$1$$$, the discontent of the leader increases by $$$c \cdot x$$$, where $$$c$$$ is some fixed constant, and $$$x$$$ is the number of minutes it took the person to reach the crossroad number $$$1$$$;  whenever $$$x$$$ members of the organization walk along the same street at the same moment in the same direction, $$$dx^2$$$ is added to the discontent, where $$$d$$$ is some fixed constant. This is not cumulative: for example, if two persons are walking along the same street in the same direction at the same moment, then $$$4d$$$ is added to the discontent, not $$$5d$$$. Before sending a message about the meeting, the leader can tell each member of the organization which path they should choose and where they should wait. Help the leader to establish a plan for every member of the organization so they all reach the crossroad $$$1$$$, and the discontent is minimized.
problem_description.input_spec: The first line of the input contains five integer numbers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$, $$$k$$$, $$$c$$$ and $$$d$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 50$$$, $$$n - 1 \le m \le 50$$$, $$$1 \le k, c, d \le 50$$$) — the number of crossroads, the number of streets, the number of persons invited to the meeting and the constants affecting the discontent, respectively. The second line contains $$$k$$$ numbers $$$a_1$$$, $$$a_2$$$, ..., $$$a_k$$$ ($$$2 \le a_i \le n$$$) — the crossroads where the members of the organization live. Then $$$m$$$ lines follow, each denoting a bidirectional street. Each line contains two integers $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$ ($$$1 \le x_i, y_i \le n$$$, $$$x_i \ne y_i$$$) denoting a street connecting crossroads $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$. There may be multiple streets connecting the same pair of crossroads. It is guaranteed that every crossroad can be reached from every other crossroad using the given streets.
problem_description.output_spec: Print one integer: the minimum discontent of the leader after everyone reaches crossroad $$$1$$$.
problem_description.notes: NoteThe best course of action in the first test is the following:  the first person goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the second person waits one minute on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the third person waits two minutes on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the fourth person waits three minutes on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting.

        self.rev = rev

    def __init__(self, n):
        self.adj = [[] for _ in range(n)]
        self.dist = [INF] * n
        self.prevv = [0] * n
        self.preve = [0] * n
        self.source = 0
        self.sink = 0
    
    def addEdge(self, u, v, cap, cost):
        self.adj[u].append(Edge(v, cap, cost, len(self.adj[v])))
        self.adj[v].append(Edge(u, 0, -cost, len(self.adj[u]) - 1))
    
    def spfa(self):
        self.dist = [INF] * len(self.dist)
        self.dist[self.source] = 0
        inq = [False] * len(self.adj)
        q = deque()
        q.append(self.source)
        inq[self.source] = True
        
        while q:
            u = q.popleft()
            inq[u] = False
            
            for i in range(len(self.adj[u])):
                e = self.adj[u][i]
                if e.capacity > 0 and self.dist[e.to] > self.dist[u] + e.cost:
                    self.dist[e.to] = self.dist[u] + e.cost
                    self.prevv[e.to] = u
                    self.preve[e.to] = i
                    if not inq[e.to]:
                        inq[e.to] = True
                        q.append(e.to)
        
        if self.dist[self.sink] == INF:
            return (0, False)
        
        flow = INF

        while v != self.source:

        v = self.sink
        while v != self.source:
            e = self.adj[self.prevv[v]][self.preve[v]]
            e.capacity -= flow
            self.adj[v][e.rev].capacity += flow
            v = self.prevv[v]
        
        return (self.dist[self.sink] * flow, True)

problem_description.description: The leader of some very secretive organization has decided to invite all other members to a meeting. All members of the organization live in the same town which can be represented as $$$n$$$ crossroads connected by $$$m$$$ two-directional streets. The meeting will be held in the leader's house near the crossroad $$$1$$$. There are $$$k$$$ members of the organization invited to the meeting; $$$i$$$-th of them lives near the crossroad $$$a_i$$$. All members of the organization receive the message about the meeting at the same moment and start moving to the location where the meeting is held. In the beginning of each minute each person is located at some crossroad. He or she can either wait a minute at this crossroad, or spend a minute to walk from the current crossroad along some street to another crossroad (obviously, it is possible to start walking along the street only if it begins or ends at the current crossroad). In the beginning of the first minute each person is at the crossroad where he or she lives. As soon as a person reaches the crossroad number $$$1$$$, he or she immediately comes to the leader's house and attends the meeting.Obviously, the leader wants all other members of the organization to come up as early as possible. But, since the organization is very secretive, the leader does not want to attract much attention. Let's denote the discontent of the leader as follows  initially the discontent is $$$0$$$;  whenever a person reaches the crossroad number $$$1$$$, the discontent of the leader increases by $$$c \cdot x$$$, where $$$c$$$ is some fixed constant, and $$$x$$$ is the number of minutes it took the person to reach the crossroad number $$$1$$$;  whenever $$$x$$$ members of the organization walk along the same street at the same moment in the same direction, $$$dx^2$$$ is added to the discontent, where $$$d$$$ is some fixed constant. This is not cumulative: for example, if two persons are walking along the same street in the same direction at the same moment, then $$$4d$$$ is added to the discontent, not $$$5d$$$. Before sending a message about the meeting, the leader can tell each member of the organization which path they should choose and where they should wait. Help the leader to establish a plan for every member of the organization so they all reach the crossroad $$$1$$$, and the discontent is minimized.
problem_description.input_spec: The first line of the input contains five integer numbers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$, $$$k$$$, $$$c$$$ and $$$d$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 50$$$, $$$n - 1 \le m \le 50$$$, $$$1 \le k, c, d \le 50$$$) — the number of crossroads, the number of streets, the number of persons invited to the meeting and the constants affecting the discontent, respectively. The second line contains $$$k$$$ numbers $$$a_1$$$, $$$a_2$$$, ..., $$$a_k$$$ ($$$2 \le a_i \le n$$$) — the crossroads where the members of the organization live. Then $$$m$$$ lines follow, each denoting a bidirectional street. Each line contains two integers $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$ ($$$1 \le x_i, y_i \le n$$$, $$$x_i \ne y_i$$$) denoting a street connecting crossroads $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$. There may be multiple streets connecting the same pair of crossroads. It is guaranteed that every crossroad can be reached from every other crossroad using the given streets.
problem_description.output_spec: Print one integer: the minimum discontent of the leader after everyone reaches crossroad $$$1$$$.
problem_description.notes: NoteThe best course of action in the first test is the following:  the first person goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the second person waits one minute on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the third person waits two minutes on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the fourth person waits three minutes on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting.

import sys
from collections import deque

def main():
    inf = 0x3f3f3f3f
    Z = 100
    N = Z * Z
    M = Z * Z * Z
    
    # Initialize graph structures
    head = [-1] * N
    to = [0] * M
    ct = [0] * M
    w = [0] * M
    nt = [0] * M
    tot = 0
    
    def add(u, v, flow, cost):
        nonlocal tot
        # Forward edge
        to[tot] = v
        ct[tot] = cost
        w[tot] = flow
        nt[tot] = head[u]
        head[u] = tot
        tot += 1
        
        # Backward edge
        to[tot] = u
        ct[tot] = -cost
        w[tot] = 0
        nt[tot] = head[v]
        head[v] = tot
        tot += 1
    
    def spfa(s, t):
        d = [inf] * N
        vis = [0] * N
        pre = [-1] * N
        id_arr = [-1] * N
        
        d[s] = 0
        q = deque([s])
        
        while q:
            u = q.popleft()
            vis[u] = 0
            i = head[u]
            while i != -1:
                if w[i] > 0 and d[to[i]] > d[u] + ct[i]:
                    d[to[i]] = d[u] + ct[i]
                    pre[to[i]] = u
                    id_arr[to[i]] = i
                    if not vis[to[i]]:
                        vis[to[i]] = 1
                        q.append(to[i])
                i = nt[i]
        
        return d[t] < inf
    
    def min_cost_flow(s, t):
        total_cost = 0
        while spfa(s, t):
            min_flow = inf
            i = t
            while i != s:
                min_flow = min(min_flow, w[id_arr[i]])
                i = pre[i]
            
            i = t
            while i != s:
                w[id_arr[i]] -= min_flow
                w[id_arr[i] ^ 1] += min_flow
                i = pre[i]
            
            total_cost += d[t] * min_flow
        
        return total_cost
    
    # Read input
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    idx = 0
    n = int(data[idx]); idx += 1
    m = int(data[idx]); idx += 1
    k = int(data[idx]); idx += 1
    c = int(data[idx]); idx += 1
    d_val = int(data[idx]); idx += 1
    
    s = 0
    t = n * 100 + 1
    
    # Connect time points to sink
    for i in range(1, 101):
        add(i, t, 100, 0)
    
    # Connect source to starting points
    for _ in range(k):
        v = int(data[idx]); idx += 1
        add(s, (v-1)*100+1, 1, 0)
    
    # Connect consecutive time points within each node
    for i in range(1, n+1):
        for j in range(1, 100):
            add((i-1)*100 + j, (i-1)*100 + j + 1, 100, c)
    
    # Process edges
    for _ in range(m):
        u = int(data[idx]); idx += 1
        v = int(data[idx]); idx += 1
        
        for j in range(1, 100):
            idx1 = (u-1) * 100 + j
            idx2 = (v-1) * 100 + j + 1
            for k_val in range(1, 21):
                cost = c + (k_val * k_val - (k_val-1) * (k_val-1)) * d_val
                add(idx1, idx2, 1, cost)
        
        for j in range(1, 100):
            idx1 = (v-1) * 100 + j
            idx2 = (u-1) * 100 + j + 1
            for k_val in range(1, 21):
                cost = c + (k_val * k_val - (k_val-1) * (k_val-1)) * d_val
                add(idx1, idx2, 1, cost)
    
    print(min_cost_flow(s, t))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

problem_description.description: The leader of some very secretive organization has decided to invite all other members to a meeting. All members of the organization live in the same town which can be represented as $$$n$$$ crossroads connected by $$$m$$$ two-directional streets. The meeting will be held in the leader's house near the crossroad $$$1$$$. There are $$$k$$$ members of the organization invited to the meeting; $$$i$$$-th of them lives near the crossroad $$$a_i$$$. All members of the organization receive the message about the meeting at the same moment and start moving to the location where the meeting is held. In the beginning of each minute each person is located at some crossroad. He or she can either wait a minute at this crossroad, or spend a minute to walk from the current crossroad along some street to another crossroad (obviously, it is possible to start walking along the street only if it begins or ends at the current crossroad). In the beginning of the first minute each person is at the crossroad where he or she lives. As soon as a person reaches the crossroad number $$$1$$$, he or she immediately comes to the leader's house and attends the meeting.Obviously, the leader wants all other members of the organization to come up as early as possible. But, since the organization is very secretive, the leader does not want to attract much attention. Let's denote the discontent of the leader as follows  initially the discontent is $$$0$$$;  whenever a person reaches the crossroad number $$$1$$$, the discontent of the leader increases by $$$c \cdot x$$$, where $$$c$$$ is some fixed constant, and $$$x$$$ is the number of minutes it took the person to reach the crossroad number $$$1$$$;  whenever $$$x$$$ members of the organization walk along the same street at the same moment in the same direction, $$$dx^2$$$ is added to the discontent, where $$$d$$$ is some fixed constant. This is not cumulative: for example, if two persons are walking along the same street in the same direction at the same moment, then $$$4d$$$ is added to the discontent, not $$$5d$$$. Before sending a message about the meeting, the leader can tell each member of the organization which path they should choose and where they should wait. Help the leader to establish a plan for every member of the organization so they all reach the crossroad $$$1$$$, and the discontent is minimized.
problem_description.input_spec: The first line of the input contains five integer numbers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$, $$$k$$$, $$$c$$$ and $$$d$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 50$$$, $$$n - 1 \le m \le 50$$$, $$$1 \le k, c, d \le 50$$$) — the number of crossroads, the number of streets, the number of persons invited to the meeting and the constants affecting the discontent, respectively. The second line contains $$$k$$$ numbers $$$a_1$$$, $$$a_2$$$, ..., $$$a_k$$$ ($$$2 \le a_i \le n$$$) — the crossroads where the members of the organization live. Then $$$m$$$ lines follow, each denoting a bidirectional street. Each line contains two integers $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$ ($$$1 \le x_i, y_i \le n$$$, $$$x_i \ne y_i$$$) denoting a street connecting crossroads $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$. There may be multiple streets connecting the same pair of crossroads. It is guaranteed that every crossroad can be reached from every other crossroad using the given streets.
problem_description.output_spec: Print one integer: the minimum discontent of the leader after everyone reaches crossroad $$$1$$$.
problem_description.notes: NoteThe best course of action in the first test is the following:  the first person goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the second person waits one minute on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the third person waits two minutes on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the fourth person waits three minutes on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting.

import sys
from collections import deque

class MCMF:
    def __init__(self):
        self.N = 30000
        self.M = 7010010
        self.h = [-1] * self.N
        self.ing = [0] * self.N
        self.pre = [0] * self.N
        self.to = [0] * self.M
        self.ne = [0] * self.M
        self.e = 0
        self.s = 0
        self.t = 0
        self.n = 0
        self.cap = [0] * self.M
        self.cost = [0] * self.M
        self.flow = 0
        self.mincost = 0

    def ini(self, _n=None):
        if _n is None:
            _n = self.N
        self.h = [-1] * _n
        self.e = 0
        self.n = _n

    def liu(self, u, v, c, w):
        self.to[self.e] = v
        self.ne[self.e] = self.h[u]
        self.cap[self.e] = c
        self.cost[self.e] = w
        self.h[u] = self.e
        self.e += 1

    def link(self, u, v, c, w):
        self.liu(u, v, c, w)
        self.liu(v, u, 0, -w)

    def spfa(self):
        dis = [float('inf')] * self.n
        Q = deque()
        Q.append(self.s)
        self.ing[self.s] = 1
        dis[self.s] = 0

        while Q:
            c = Q.popleft()
            self.ing[c] = 0
            k = self.h[c]
            while k != -1:
                if self.cap[k] > 0:
                    v = self.to[k]
                    if dis[c] + self.cost[k] < dis[v]:
                        dis[v] = dis[c] + self.cost[k]
                        self.pre[v] = k
                        if not self.ing[v]:
                            Q.append(v)
                            self.ing[v] = 1
                k = self.ne[k]

        return dis[self.t] != float('inf')

    def run(self, _s, _t):
        self.s = _s
        self.t = _t
        self.flow = 0
        self.mincost = 0

        while self.spfa():
            pl = float('inf')
            p = self.t
            while p != self.s:
                k = self.pre[p]
                pl = min(pl, self.cap[k])
                p = self.to[k ^ 1]

            p = self.t
            while p != self.s:
                k = self.pre[p]
                self.cap[k] -= pl
                self.cap[k ^ 1] += pl
                p = self.to[k ^ 1]

            self.mincost += pl * dis[self.t]
            self.flow += pl

        return (self.flow, self.mincost)


def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    if not data:
        return
    
    it = iter(data)
    n = int(next(it))
    m = int(next(it))
    k = int(next(it))
    c = int(next(it))
    d = int(next(it))
    
    a = [0] * (k + 1)
    for i in range(1, k + 1):
        a[i] = int(next(it))
    
    flow = MCMF()
    flow.ini(50 * 50 * 4 + 10)
    
    s = flow.n - 2
    t = flow.n - 3
    
    cnt = 0
    mx = 100
    id = [[0] * (mx + 1) for _ in range(55)]
    
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        for j in range(mx + 1):
            cnt += 1
            id[i][j] = cnt
    
    for _ in range(1, m + 1):
        u = int(next(it))
        v = int(next(it))
        for j in range(mx):
            for h_val in range(1, k + 1):
                tmp = h_val * h_val * d - (h_val - 1) * (h_val - 1) * d
                flow.link(id[u][j], id[v][j + 1], 1, c + tmp)
                flow.link(id[v][j], id[u][j + 1], 1, c + tmp)
    
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        for j in range(mx):
            flow.link(id[i][j], id[i][j + 1], float('inf'), c)
    
    for i in range(1, k + 1):
        flow.link(s, id[a[i]][0], 1, 0)
    
    for j in range(1, mx + 1):
        flow.link(id[1][j], t, float('inf'), 0)
    
    result = flow.run(s, t)
    ans = result[1]
    print(ans)

    main()

import sys
from collections import deque

class MinCostMaxFlow:
    MAXN = 30000
    MAXM = 7010010

    def __init__(self):
        self.head = [-1] * self.MAXN
        self.inq = [0] * self.MAXN
        self.prevv = [0] * self.MAXN
        self.to = [0] * self.MAXM
        self.nxt = [0] * self.MAXM
        self.idx = 0
        self.src = 0
        self.dst = 0
        self.nodes = 0
        self.cap = [0] * self.MAXM
        self.cost = [0] * self.MAXM
        self.total_flow = 0
        self.total_cost = 0

    def init(self, n=None):
        if n is None:
            n = self.MAXN
        self.head = [-1] * n
        self.nodes = n
        self.idx = 0

    def add_edge(self, u, v, c, w):
        self.to[self.idx] = v
        self.nxt[self.idx] = self.head[u]
        self.cap[self.idx] = c
        self.cost[self.idx] = w
        self.head[u] = self.idx
        self.idx += 1

    def add_bidirectional(self, u, v, c, w):
        self.add_edge(u, v, c, w)
        self.add_edge(v, u, 0, -w)

    def spfa(self):
        dist = [float('inf')] * self.nodes
        dist[self.src] = 0
        q = deque([self.src])
        self.inq[self.src] = 1

        while q:
            u = q.popleft()
            self.inq[u] = 0

            e = self.head[u]
            while e != -1:
                if self.cap[e] > 0:
                    v = self.to[e]
                    if dist[u] + self.cost[e] < dist[v]:
                        dist[v] = dist[u] + self.cost[e]
                        self.prevv[v] = e
                        if not self.inq[v]:
                            q.append(v)
                            self.inq[v] = 1
                e = self.nxt[e]

        return dist[self.dst] != float('inf')

    def compute(self, s, t):
        self.src = s
        self.dst = t
        self.total_flow = 0

from collections import deque

INF = float('inf')

class Edge:
    __slots__ = ('to', 'next', 'capacity', 'cost')
    def __init__(self, to, next_edge, capacity, cost):
        self.to = to
        self.next = next_edge
        self.capacity = capacity
        self.cost = cost

class MCMF:
    def __init__(self, max_nodes):
        self.MAX_NODES = max_nodes
        self.head = [-1] * max_nodes
        self.prevv = [0] * max_nodes
        self.inq = [0] * max_nodes
        self.edges = []
        self.dist = [INF] * max_nodes
        self.idx = 0
        self.src = 0
        self.dst = 0
        self.node_count = 0

    def init(self, n):
        self.head = [-1] * n
        self.idx = 0
        self.node_count = n

    def add_edge(self, u, v, cap, w):
        self.edges.append(Edge(v, self.head[u], cap, w))
        self.head[u] = self.idx
        self.idx += 1

    def add_bidirectional(self, u, v, cap, w):
        self.add_edge(u, v, cap, w)
        self.add_edge(v, u, 0, -w)

    def spfa(self):
        self.dist = [INF] * self.node_count
        q = deque()
        q.append(self.src)
        self.dist[self.src] = 0
        self.inq = [0] * self.node_count
        self.inq[self.src] = 1

        while q:
            u = q.popleft()
            self.inq[u] = 0

            e = self.head[u]
            while e != -1:
                edge = self.edges[e]
                if edge.capacity > 0:
                    v = edge.to
                    nd = self.dist[u] + edge.cost
                    if nd < self.dist[v]:
                        self.dist[v] = nd
                        self.prevv[v] = e
                        if not self.inq[v]:
                            q.append(v)
                            self.inq[v] = 1
                e = self.edges[e].next

        return self.dist[self.dst] != INF

    def run(self, s, t):
        self.src = s
        self.dst = t
        total_flow = 0
        total_cost = 0

        while self.spfa():
            bottleneck = INF
            e = 0
            v = self.dst
            path_edges = []
            while v != self.src:
                e = self.prevv[v]
                path_edges.append(e)
                bottleneck = min(bottleneck, self.edges[e].capacity)
                v = self.edges[e ^ 1].to

            for e in path_edges:
                self.edges[e].capacity -= bottleneck
                self.edges[e ^ 1].capacity += bottleneck

            total_cost += bottleneck * self.dist[self.dst]
            total_flow += bottleneck

        return total_flow, total_cost

import heapq

def main():
    input = sys.stdin.read
    data = input().split()
    
    idx = 0
    n = int(data[idx]); idx += 1
    m = int(data[idx]); idx += 1
    k = int(data[idx]); idx += 1
    c = int(data[idx]); idx += 1
    d = int(data[idx]); idx += 1
    
    a = [0] * (k + 1)
    for i in range(1, k + 1):
        a[i] = int(data[idx]); idx += 1
    
    MAX_LEVEL = 100
    MAX_NODES = 50 * 50 * 4 + 10
    source = MAX_NODES - 2
    sink = MAX_NODES - 3
    
    # Initialize graph as adjacency list
    # Each entry: [to, capacity, cost, reverse_index]
    graph = [[] for _ in range(MAX_NODES)]
    
    def add_edge(from_node, to_node, cap, cost):
        graph[from_node].append([to_node, cap, cost, len(graph[to_node])])
        graph[to_node].append([from_node, 0, -cost, len(graph[from_node]) - 1])
    
    # node_id[i][j] = node index for position i at level j
    node_id = [[0] * (MAX_LEVEL + 1) for _ in range(n + 1)]
    counter = 0
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        for j in range(MAX_LEVEL + 1):
            counter += 1
            node_id[i][j] = counter

    for _ in range(m):
        u = int(data[idx]); idx += 1
        v = int(data[idx]); idx += 1
        for level in range(MAX_LEVEL):
            for step in range(1, k + 1):
                delta = step * step * d - (step - 1) * (step - 1) * d
                add_edge(node_id[u][level], node_id[v][level + 1], 1, c + delta)
                add_edge(node_id[v][level], node_id[u][level + 1], 1, c + delta)
    
    # Self-loop edges
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        for level in range(MAX_LEVEL):
            add_edge(node_id[i][level], node_id[i][level + 1], 10**9, c)
    
    # Source connections
    for i in range(1, k + 1):
        add_edge(source, node_id[a[i]][0], 1, 0)
    
    # Sink connections
    for level in range(1, MAX_LEVEL + 1):
        add_edge(node_id[1][level], sink, 10**9, 0)
    
    # MCMF algorithm using Bellman-Ford (SPFA)
    def min_cost_flow(src, dst):
        INF = 10**18
        total_flow = 0
        total_cost = 0
        
        while True:
            dist = [INF] * MAX_NODES
            prevv = [-1] * MAX_NODES
            preve = [-1] * MAX_NODES
            dist[src] = 0
            in_queue = [False] * MAX_NODES
            queue = [src]
            in_queue[src] = True
            
            while queue:
                v = queue.pop(0)
                in_queue[v] = False
                for i, (to, cap, cost, rev) in enumerate(graph[v]):
                    if cap > 0 and dist[to] > dist[v] + cost:
                        dist[to] = dist[v] + cost
                        prevv[to] = v
                        preve[to] = i
                        if not in_queue[to]:
                            queue.append(to)
                            in_queue[to] = True
            
            if dist[dst] == INF:
                break
            
            f = 10**9
            v = dst
            while v != src:
                u = prevv[v]
                e_idx = preve[v]
                f = min(f, graph[u][e_idx][1])
                v = u
            
            total_flow += f
            total_cost += f * dist[dst]
            
            v = dst
            while v != src:
                u = prevv[v]
                e_idx = preve[v]
                graph[u][e_idx][1] -= f
                rev_idx = graph[u][e_idx][3]
                graph[v][rev_idx][1] += f
                v = u
        
        return (total_flow, total_cost)
    
    result = min_cost_flow(source, sink)
    print(result[1])

problem_description.description: The leader of some very secretive organization has decided to invite all other members to a meeting. All members of the organization live in the same town which can be represented as $$$n$$$ crossroads connected by $$$m$$$ two-directional streets. The meeting will be held in the leader's house near the crossroad $$$1$$$. There are $$$k$$$ members of the organization invited to the meeting; $$$i$$$-th of them lives near the crossroad $$$a_i$$$. All members of the organization receive the message about the meeting at the same moment and start moving to the location where the meeting is held. In the beginning of each minute each person is located at some crossroad. He or she can either wait a minute at this crossroad, or spend a minute to walk from the current crossroad along some street to another crossroad (obviously, it is possible to start walking along the street only if it begins or ends at the current crossroad). In the beginning of the first minute each person is at the crossroad where he or she lives. As soon as a person reaches the crossroad number $$$1$$$, he or she immediately comes to the leader's house and attends the meeting.Obviously, the leader wants all other members of the organization to come up as early as possible. But, since the organization is very secretive, the leader does not want to attract much attention. Let's denote the discontent of the leader as follows  initially the discontent is $$$0$$$;  whenever a person reaches the crossroad number $$$1$$$, the discontent of the leader increases by $$$c \cdot x$$$, where $$$c$$$ is some fixed constant, and $$$x$$$ is the number of minutes it took the person to reach the crossroad number $$$1$$$;  whenever $$$x$$$ members of the organization walk along the same street at the same moment in the same direction, $$$dx^2$$$ is added to the discontent, where $$$d$$$ is some fixed constant. This is not cumulative: for example, if two persons are walking along the same street in the same direction at the same moment, then $$$4d$$$ is added to the discontent, not $$$5d$$$. Before sending a message about the meeting, the leader can tell each member of the organization which path they should choose and where they should wait. Help the leader to establish a plan for every member of the organization so they all reach the crossroad $$$1$$$, and the discontent is minimized.
problem_description.input_spec: The first line of the input contains five integer numbers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$, $$$k$$$, $$$c$$$ and $$$d$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 50$$$, $$$n - 1 \le m \le 50$$$, $$$1 \le k, c, d \le 50$$$) — the number of crossroads, the number of streets, the number of persons invited to the meeting and the constants affecting the discontent, respectively. The second line contains $$$k$$$ numbers $$$a_1$$$, $$$a_2$$$, ..., $$$a_k$$$ ($$$2 \le a_i \le n$$$) — the crossroads where the members of the organization live. Then $$$m$$$ lines follow, each denoting a bidirectional street. Each line contains two integers $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$ ($$$1 \le x_i, y_i \le n$$$, $$$x_i \ne y_i$$$) denoting a street connecting crossroads $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$. There may be multiple streets connecting the same pair of crossroads. It is guaranteed that every crossroad can be reached from every other crossroad using the given streets.
problem_description.output_spec: Print one integer: the minimum discontent of the leader after everyone reaches crossroad $$$1$$$.
problem_description.notes: NoteThe best course of action in the first test is the following:  the first person goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the second person waits one minute on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the third person waits two minutes on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the fourth person waits three minutes on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting.

class MinCostMaxFlowSolver:
    def __init__(self):
        self.numVertices = 0
        self.MAXN = 6555
        self.potential = [0] * (self.MAXN + 5)
        self.dist = [0] * (self.MAXN + 5)
        self.prevVertex = [0] * (self.MAXN + 5)
        self.prevEdge = [0] * (self.MAXN + 5)
        self.adjList = defaultdict(list)
    
    def initialize(self, n):
        self.numVertices = n
        self.adjList = defaultdict(list)
    
    def insertEdge(self, from_node, to_node, cap, cst):
        # Forward edge
        forward_index = len(self.adjList[to_node])
        reverse_index = len(self.adjList[from_node])
        self.adjList[from_node].append(Edge(to_node, cap, cst, forward_index))
        # Backward edge
        self.adjList[to_node].append(Edge(from_node, 0, -cst, reverse_index))
    
    def calculate(self, source, sink, flowNeeded):
        totalFlow = 0
        totalCost = 0
        # Reset potential
        self.potential = [0] * (self.MAXN + 5)
        
        while flowNeeded > 0:
            # Dijkstra's algorithm with priority queue
            self.dist = [float('inf')] * (self.MAXN + 5)
            self.dist[source] = 0
            pq = [(0, source)]
            visited = set()
            
            while pq:
                d, u = heapq.heappop(pq)
                if u in visited:
                    continue
                visited.add(u)
                if d != self.dist[u]:
                    continue
                for i, e in enumerate(self.adjList[u]):
                    if e.capacity > 0 and self.dist[e.target] > self.dist[u] + e.cost + self.potential[u] - self.potential[e.target]:
                        self.dist[e.target] = self.dist[u] + e.cost + self.potential[u] - self.potential[e.target]
                        self.prevVertex[e.target] = u
                        self.prevEdge[e.target] = i
                        heapq.heappush(pq, (self.dist[e.target], e.target))
            
            if self.dist[sink] == float('inf'):
                break
            
            # Update potential
            for i in range(self.numVertices + 1):
                self.potential[i] += self.dist[i]
            
            # Find the minimum capacity along the path
            flow = flowNeeded
            v = sink
            while v != source:
                u = self.prevVertex[v]
                edge_index = self.prevEdge[v]
                edge = self.adjList[u][edge_index]
                flow = min(flow, edge.capacity)
                v = u
            
            flowNeeded -= flow
            totalFlow += flow
            totalCost += flow * self.potential[sink]
            
            # Update capacities
            v = sink
            while v != source:
                u = self.prevVertex[v]
                edge_index = self.prevEdge[v]
                edge = self.adjList[u][edge_index]
                edge.capacity -= flow
                reverse_edge = self.adjList[v][edge.reverseIndex]
                reverse_edge.capacity += flow
                v = u

problem_description.description: The leader of some very secretive organization has decided to invite all other members to a meeting. All members of the organization live in the same town which can be represented as $$$n$$$ crossroads connected by $$$m$$$ two-directional streets. The meeting will be held in the leader's house near the crossroad $$$1$$$. There are $$$k$$$ members of the organization invited to the meeting; $$$i$$$-th of them lives near the crossroad $$$a_i$$$. All members of the organization receive the message about the meeting at the same moment and start moving to the location where the meeting is held. In the beginning of each minute each person is located at some crossroad. He or she can either wait a minute at this crossroad, or spend a minute to walk from the current crossroad along some street to another crossroad (obviously, it is possible to start walking along the street only if it begins or ends at the current crossroad). In the beginning of the first minute each person is at the crossroad where he or she lives. As soon as a person reaches the crossroad number $$$1$$$, he or she immediately comes to the leader's house and attends the meeting.Obviously, the leader wants all other members of the organization to come up as early as possible. But, since the organization is very secretive, the leader does not want to attract much attention. Let's denote the discontent of the leader as follows  initially the discontent is $$$0$$$;  whenever a person reaches the crossroad number $$$1$$$, the discontent of the leader increases by $$$c \cdot x$$$, where $$$c$$$ is some fixed constant, and $$$x$$$ is the number of minutes it took the person to reach the crossroad number $$$1$$$;  whenever $$$x$$$ members of the organization walk along the same street at the same moment in the same direction, $$$dx^2$$$ is added to the discontent, where $$$d$$$ is some fixed constant. This is not cumulative: for example, if two persons are walking along the same street in the same direction at the same moment, then $$$4d$$$ is added to the discontent, not $$$5d$$$. Before sending a message about the meeting, the leader can tell each member of the organization which path they should choose and where they should wait. Help the leader to establish a plan for every member of the organization so they all reach the crossroad $$$1$$$, and the discontent is minimized.
problem_description.input_spec: The first line of the input contains five integer numbers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$, $$$k$$$, $$$c$$$ and $$$d$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 50$$$, $$$n - 1 \le m \le 50$$$, $$$1 \le k, c, d \le 50$$$) — the number of crossroads, the number of streets, the number of persons invited to the meeting and the constants affecting the discontent, respectively. The second line contains $$$k$$$ numbers $$$a_1$$$, $$$a_2$$$, ..., $$$a_k$$$ ($$$2 \le a_i \le n$$$) — the crossroads where the members of the organization live. Then $$$m$$$ lines follow, each denoting a bidirectional street. Each line contains two integers $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$ ($$$1 \le x_i, y_i \le n$$$, $$$x_i \ne y_i$$$) denoting a street connecting crossroads $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$. There may be multiple streets connecting the same pair of crossroads. It is guaranteed that every crossroad can be reached from every other crossroad using the given streets.
problem_description.output_spec: Print one integer: the minimum discontent of the leader after everyone reaches crossroad $$$1$$$.
problem_description.notes: NoteThe best course of action in the first test is the following:  the first person goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the second person waits one minute on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the third person waits two minutes on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the fourth person waits three minutes on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting.

    __slots__ = ('u', 'v', 'cap', 'flow', 'cost')
    def __init__(self, u, v, cap, flow, cost):
        self.u = u
        self.v = v
        self.cap = cap
        self.flow = flow
        self.cost = cost
    
    def rem(self):
        return self.cap - self.flow

nodes = MAXN
g = [[] for _ in range(MAXN)]
e = []

def add_edge(u, v, cap, cost):
    if DEBUG:
        dem = str(u)
        pen = str(v)
        if u == SRC:
            dem = "SRC"
        if u == SNC:
            dem = "SINC"
        if v == SRC:
            pen = "SRC"
        if v == SNC:
            pen = "SINC"
        print(f"add edge: {dem} {pen} {cap} {cost}")
    
    idx1 = len(e)
    g[u].append(idx1)
    e.append(Edge(u, v, cap, 0, cost))
    
    idx2 = len(e)
    g[v].append(idx2)
    e.append(Edge(v, u, 0, 0, -cost))

def flow(s, t):
    global mxflow, mncost
    in_queue = [False] * nodes
    mxflow = 0
    mncost = 0
    
    while True:
        dist = [INFCOSTO] * nodes
        dist[s] = 0
        pre = [-1] * nodes
        pre[s] = 0
        cap = [0] * nodes
        cap[s] = INFFLUJO
        q = deque()
        q.append(s)
        in_queue[s] = True
        
        while q:
            u = q.popleft()
            in_queue[u] = False
            
            for idx in g[u]:
                E = e[idx]
                if E.rem() > 0 and dist[E.v] > dist[u] + E.cost + 1e-9:
                    dist[E.v] = dist[u] + E.cost
                    pre[E.v] = idx
                    cap[E.v] = min(cap[u], E.rem())
                    if not in_queue[E.v]:
                        q.append(E.v)
                        in_queue[E.v] = True
        
        if pre[t] < 0:
            break
        
        mxflow += cap[t]
        mncost += cap[t] * dist[t]
        
        v = t
        while v != s:
            edge_idx = pre[v]
            e[edge_idx].flow += cap[t]
            e[edge_idx ^ 1].flow -= cap[t]
            v = e[edge_idx].u

problem_description.description: The leader of some very secretive organization has decided to invite all other members to a meeting. All members of the organization live in the same town which can be represented as $$$n$$$ crossroads connected by $$$m$$$ two-directional streets. The meeting will be held in the leader's house near the crossroad $$$1$$$. There are $$$k$$$ members of the organization invited to the meeting; $$$i$$$-th of them lives near the crossroad $$$a_i$$$. All members of the organization receive the message about the meeting at the same moment and start moving to the location where the meeting is held. In the beginning of each minute each person is located at some crossroad. He or she can either wait a minute at this crossroad, or spend a minute to walk from the current crossroad along some street to another crossroad (obviously, it is possible to start walking along the street only if it begins or ends at the current crossroad). In the beginning of the first minute each person is at the crossroad where he or she lives. As soon as a person reaches the crossroad number $$$1$$$, he or she immediately comes to the leader's house and attends the meeting.Obviously, the leader wants all other members of the organization to come up as early as possible. But, since the organization is very secretive, the leader does not want to attract much attention. Let's denote the discontent of the leader as follows  initially the discontent is $$$0$$$;  whenever a person reaches the crossroad number $$$1$$$, the discontent of the leader increases by $$$c \cdot x$$$, where $$$c$$$ is some fixed constant, and $$$x$$$ is the number of minutes it took the person to reach the crossroad number $$$1$$$;  whenever $$$x$$$ members of the organization walk along the same street at the same moment in the same direction, $$$dx^2$$$ is added to the discontent, where $$$d$$$ is some fixed constant. This is not cumulative: for example, if two persons are walking along the same street in the same direction at the same moment, then $$$4d$$$ is added to the discontent, not $$$5d$$$. Before sending a message about the meeting, the leader can tell each member of the organization which path they should choose and where they should wait. Help the leader to establish a plan for every member of the organization so they all reach the crossroad $$$1$$$, and the discontent is minimized.
problem_description.input_spec: The first line of the input contains five integer numbers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$, $$$k$$$, $$$c$$$ and $$$d$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 50$$$, $$$n - 1 \le m \le 50$$$, $$$1 \le k, c, d \le 50$$$) — the number of crossroads, the number of streets, the number of persons invited to the meeting and the constants affecting the discontent, respectively. The second line contains $$$k$$$ numbers $$$a_1$$$, $$$a_2$$$, ..., $$$a_k$$$ ($$$2 \le a_i \le n$$$) — the crossroads where the members of the organization live. Then $$$m$$$ lines follow, each denoting a bidirectional street. Each line contains two integers $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$ ($$$1 \le x_i, y_i \le n$$$, $$$x_i \ne y_i$$$) denoting a street connecting crossroads $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$. There may be multiple streets connecting the same pair of crossroads. It is guaranteed that every crossroad can be reached from every other crossroad using the given streets.
problem_description.output_spec: Print one integer: the minimum discontent of the leader after everyone reaches crossroad $$$1$$$.

problem_description.description: The leader of some very secretive organization has decided to invite all other members to a meeting. All members of the organization live in the same town which can be represented as $$$n$$$ crossroads connected by $$$m$$$ two-directional streets. The meeting will be held in the leader's house near the crossroad $$$1$$$. There are $$$k$$$ members of the organization invited to the meeting; $$$i$$$-th of them lives near the crossroad $$$a_i$$$. All members of the organization receive the message about the meeting at the same moment and start moving to the location where the meeting is held. In the beginning of each minute each person is located at some crossroad. He or she can either wait a minute at this crossroad, or spend a minute to walk from the current crossroad along some street to another crossroad (obviously, it is possible to start walking along the street only if it begins or ends at the current crossroad). In the beginning of the first minute each person is at the crossroad where he or she lives. As soon as a person reaches the crossroad number $$$1$$$, he or she immediately comes to the leader's house and attends the meeting.Obviously, the leader wants all other members of the organization to come up as early as possible. But, since the organization is very secretive, the leader does not want to attract much attention. Let's denote the discontent of the leader as follows  initially the discontent is $$$0$$$;  whenever a person reaches the crossroad number $$$1$$$, the discontent of the leader increases by $$$c \cdot x$$$, where $$$c$$$ is some fixed constant, and $$$x$$$ is the number of minutes it took the person to reach the crossroad number $$$1$$$;  whenever $$$x$$$ members of the organization walk along the same street at the same moment in the same direction, $$$dx^2$$$ is added to the discontent, where $$$d$$$ is some fixed constant. This is not cumulative: for example, if two persons are walking along the same street in the same direction at the same moment, then $$$4d$$$ is added to the discontent, not $$$5d$$$. Before sending a message about the meeting, the leader can tell each member of the organization which path they should choose and where they should wait. Help the leader to establish a plan for every member of the organization so they all reach the crossroad $$$1$$$, and the discontent is minimized.
problem_description.input_spec: The first line of the input contains five integer numbers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$, $$$k$$$, $$$c$$$ and $$$d$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 50$$$, $$$n - 1 \le m \le 50$$$, $$$1 \le k, c, d \le 50$$$) — the number of crossroads, the number of streets, the number of persons invited to the meeting and the constants affecting the discontent, respectively. The second line contains $$$k$$$ numbers $$$a_1$$$, $$$a_2$$$, ..., $$$a_k$$$ ($$$2 \le a_i \le n$$$) — the crossroads where the members of the organization live. Then $$$m$$$ lines follow, each denoting a bidirectional street. Each line contains two integers $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$ ($$$1 \le x_i, y_i \le n$$$, $$$x_i \ne y_i$$$) denoting a street connecting crossroads $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$. There may be multiple streets connecting the same pair of crossroads. It is guaranteed that every crossroad can be reached from every other crossroad using the given streets.
problem_description.output_spec: Print one integer: the minimum discontent of the leader after everyone reaches crossroad $$$1$$$.
problem_description.notes: NoteThe best course of action in the first test is the following:  the first person goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the second person waits one minute on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the third person waits two minutes on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the fourth person waits three minutes on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting.
