problem_description.description: The leader of some very secretive organization has decided to invite all other members to a meeting. All members of the organization live in the same town which can be represented as $$$n$$$ crossroads connected by $$$m$$$ two-directional streets. The meeting will be held in the leader's house near the crossroad $$$1$$$. There are $$$k$$$ members of the organization invited to the meeting; $$$i$$$-th of them lives near the crossroad $$$a_i$$$. All members of the organization receive the message about the meeting at the same moment and start moving to the location where the meeting is held. In the beginning of each minute each person is located at some crossroad. He or she can either wait a minute at this crossroad, or spend a minute to walk from the current crossroad along some street to another crossroad (obviously, it is possible to start walking along the street only if it begins or ends at the current crossroad). In the beginning of the first minute each person is at the crossroad where he or she lives. As soon as a person reaches the crossroad number $$$1$$$, he or she immediately comes to the leader's house and attends the meeting.Obviously, the leader wants all other members of the organization to come up as early as possible. But, since the organization is very secretive, the leader does not want to attract much attention. Let's denote the discontent of the leader as follows  initially the discontent is $$$0$$$;  whenever a person reaches the crossroad number $$$1$$$, the discontent of the leader increases by $$$c \cdot x$$$, where $$$c$$$ is some fixed constant, and $$$x$$$ is the number of minutes it took the person to reach the crossroad number $$$1$$$;  whenever $$$x$$$ members of the organization walk along the same street at the same moment in the same direction, $$$dx^2$$$ is added to the discontent, where $$$d$$$ is some fixed constant. This is not cumulative: for example, if two persons are walking along the same street in the same direction at the same moment, then $$$4d$$$ is added to the discontent, not $$$5d$$$. Before sending a message about the meeting, the leader can tell each member of the organization which path they should choose and where they should wait. Help the leader to establish a plan for every member of the organization so they all reach the crossroad $$$1$$$, and the discontent is minimized.
problem_description.input_spec: The first line of the input contains five integer numbers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$, $$$k$$$, $$$c$$$ and $$$d$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 50$$$, $$$n - 1 \le m \le 50$$$, $$$1 \le k, c, d \le 50$$$) — the number of crossroads, the number of streets, the number of persons invited to the meeting and the constants affecting the discontent, respectively. The second line contains $$$k$$$ numbers $$$a_1$$$, $$$a_2$$$, ..., $$$a_k$$$ ($$$2 \le a_i \le n$$$) — the crossroads where the members of the organization live. Then $$$m$$$ lines follow, each denoting a bidirectional street. Each line contains two integers $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$ ($$$1 \le x_i, y_i \le n$$$, $$$x_i \ne y_i$$$) denoting a street connecting crossroads $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$. There may be multiple streets connecting the same pair of crossroads. It is guaranteed that every crossroad can be reached from every other crossroad using the given streets.
problem_description.output_spec: Print one integer: the minimum discontent of the leader after everyone reaches crossroad $$$1$$$.
problem_description.notes: NoteThe best course of action in the first test is the following:  the first person goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the second person waits one minute on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the third person waits two minutes on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the fourth person waits three minutes on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting.

import sys

        self.dist[self.s] = 0

        self.prev_edge[self.s] = 0

            self.edges[self.prev_edge[cur] ^ 1].flow -= flow_sent
            cur = self.edges[self.prev_edge[cur]].u
        
        return True, flow_sent, total_cost

    def compute_min_cost_flow(self, source, sink):
        self.s = source
        self.t = sink
        total_cost = 0
        total_flow = 0

        while True:
            found, flow_per_iteration, cost_per_flow = self.bellman_ford()
            if not found:
                break
            total_flow += flow_per_iteration
            total_cost += flow_per_iteration * cost_per_flow
        
        return total_flow, total_cost

All members of the organization live in the same town which can be represented as $$$n$$$ crossroads connected by $$$m$$$ two-directional streets. The meeting will be held in the leader's house near the crossroad $$$1$$$. There are $$$k$$$ members of the organization invited to the meeting; $$$i$$$-th of them lives near the crossroad $$$a_i$$$. All members of the organization receive the message about the meeting at the same moment and start moving to the location where the meeting is held. In the beginning of each minute each person is located at some crossroad. He or she can either wait a minute at this crossroad, or spend a minute to walk from the current crossroad along some street to another crossroad (obviously, it is possible to start walking along the street only if it begins or ends at the current crossroad). In the beginning of the first minute each person is at the crossroad where he or she lives. As soon as a person reaches the crossroad number $$$1$$$, he or she immediately comes to the leader's house and attends the meeting.Obviously, the leader wants all other members of the organization to come up as early as possible. But, since the organization is very secretive, the leader does not want to attract much attention. Let's denote the discontent of the leader as follows  initially the discontent is $$$0$$$;  whenever a person reaches the crossroad number $$$1$$$, the discontent of the leader increases by $$$c \cdot x$$$, where $$$c$$$ is some fixed constant, and $$$x$$$ is the number of minutes it took the person to reach the crossroad number $$$1$$$;  whenever $$$x$$$ members of the organization walk along the same street at the same moment in the same direction, $$$dx^2$$$ is added to the discontent, where $$$d$$$ is some fixed constant. This is not cumulative: for example, if two persons are walking along the same street in the same direction at the same moment, then $$$4d$$$ is added to the discontent, not $$$5d$$$. Before sending a message about the meeting, the leader can tell each member of the organization which path they should choose and where they should wait. import sys
from collections import deque

INF64 = 1000000000000000000
INF32 = 1000000000
MOD = 1000000007

def norm(x):
    x %= MOD
    if x < 0:
        x += MOD
    return x

def mul(a, b):
    return (a * b) % MOD

def binpow(a, e):
    res = 1
    while e:
        if e & 1:
            res = mul(res, a)
        a = mul(a, a)
        e >>= 1
    return res

def modinv(a):
    return binpow(a, MOD - 2)

class Edge:
    def __init__(self, to, cap, flow, cost):
        self.to = to
        self.cap = cap
        self.flow = flow
        self.cost = cost

edgeList = []
MAX_NODES = 1000007
adj = [[] for _ in range(MAX_NODES)]

dist = [INF64] * MAX_NODES
prevNode = [-1] * MAX_NODES
prevEdge = [-1] * MAX_NODES
inQ = [False] * MAX_NODES

src = MAX_NODES - 2
dst = MAX_NODES - 1

def residual(idx):
    return edgeList[idx].cap - edgeList[idx].flow

def spfa():
    global dist, prevNode, prevEdge, inQ
    dist = [INF64] * MAX_NODES
    prevNode = [-1] * MAX_NODES
    prevEdge = [-1] * MAX_NODES
    inQ = [False] * MAX_NODES
    
    dist[src] = 0
    q = deque()
    q.append(src)
    inQ[src] = True
    
    while q:
        u = q.popleft()
        inQ[u] = False
        
        for idx in adj[u]:
            if not residual(idx):
                continue
            v = edgeList[idx].to
            cost = edgeList[idx].cost
            if dist[v] > dist[u] + cost:
                dist[v] = dist[u] + cost
                prevNode[v] = u
                prevEdge[v] = idx
                if not inQ[v]:
                    inQ[v] = True
                    q.append(v)
    
    cur = dst
    while cur != src:
        edgeList[prevEdge[cur]].flow += 1
        edgeList[prevEdge[cur] ^ 1].flow -= 1
        cur = prevNode[cur]

def add_edge(u, v, cap, cost):
    adj[u].append(len(edgeList))
    edgeList.append(Edge(v, cap, 0, cost))
    adj[v].append(len(edgeList))
    edgeList.append(Edge(u, 0, 0, -cost))

def main():
    global n, m, k, c, d
    data = sys.stdin.readline().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    m = int(data[1])
    k = int(data[2])
    c = int(data[3])
    d = int(data[4])
    
    for i in range(k):
        x = int(sys.stdin.readline().strip())
        x -= 1
        add_edge(src, x, 1, 0)
    
    T = 101
    for t in range(T):
        add_edge(t * n, dst, k, t * c)
    
    for i in range(m):
        data = sys.stdin.readline().split()
        x = int(data[0])
        y = int(data[1])
        x -= 1
        y -= 1
        for t in range(T - 1):
            for j in range(k):
                add_edge(x + t * n, y + t * n + n, 1, d * (j * 2 + 1))
        for t in range(T - 1):
            for j in range(k):
                add_edge(y + t * n, x + t * n + n, 1, d * (j * 2 + 1))
    
    for i in range(n):
        for t in range(T - 1):
            add_edge(i + t * n, i + t * n + n, k, 0)
    
    ans = 0
    for i in range(k):
        spfa()
        ans += dist[dst]
    
    print(ans)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import sys
from collections import deque

MOD = 1000000007

def norm(x):
    x %= MOD
    return x if x >= 0 else x + MOD

def mul(a, b):
    return (a * b) % MOD

def binpow(a, e):
    r = 1
    while e:
        if e & 1:
            r = mul(r, a)
        a = mul(a, a)
        e >>= 1
    return r

def modinv(a):
    return binpow(a, MOD - 2)

class Edge:
    def __init__(self, to, cap, flow, cost):
        self.to = to
        self.cap = cap
        self.flow = flow
        self.cost = cost

E = []
MAXN = 1000007
G = [[] for _ in range(MAXN)]

d = [float('inf')] * MAXN
par = [-1] * MAXN
pe = [-1] * MAXN
inq = [False] * MAXN

S = MAXN - 2
T = MAXN - 1

def resCap(idx):
    return E[idx].cap - E[idx].flow

def spfa():
    global d, par, pe, inq
    d = [float('inf')] * MAXN
    par = [-1] * MAXN
    pe = [-1] * MAXN
    inq = [False] * MAXN
    
    d[S] = 0
    q = deque()
    q.append(S)
    inq[S] = True
    
    while q:
        u = q.popleft()
        inq[u] = False
        
        for idx in G[u]:
            if not resCap(idx):
                continue
            v = E[idx].to
            c = E[idx].cost
            if d[v] > d[u] + c:
                d[v] = d[u] + c
                par[v] = u
                pe[v] = idx
                if not inq[v]:
                    inq[v] = True
                    q.append(v)
    
    cur = T
    while cur != S:
        E[pe[cur]].flow += 1
        E[pe[cur] ^ 1].flow -= 1
        cur = par[cur]

def addEdge(u, v, cap, cost):
    G[u].append(len(E))
    E.append(Edge(v, cap, 0, cost))
    G[v].append(len(E))
    E.append(Edge(u, 0, 0, -cost))

def main():
    global n, m, k, c, d
    
    data = sys.stdin.readline().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    m = int(data[1])
    k = int(data[2])
    c = int(data[3])
    d_val = int(data[4])
    
    for i in range(k):
        x = int(sys.stdin.readline().strip())
        x -= 1
        addEdge(S, x, 1, 0)
    
    T_LAYERS = 101
    for t in range(T_LAYERS):
        addEdge(t * n, T, k, t * c)
    
    for i in range(m):
        data = sys.stdin.readline().split()
        x = int(data[0]) - 1
        y = int(data[1]) - 1
        for t in range(T_LAYERS - 1):
            for j in range(k):
                addEdge(x + t * n, y + t * n + n, 1, d_val * (2 * j + 1))
        for t in range(T_LAYERS - 1):
            for j in range(k):
                addEdge(y + t * n, x + t * n + n, 1, d_val * (2 * j + 1))
    
    for i in range(n):
        for t in range(T_LAYERS - 1):
            addEdge(i + t * n, i + t * n + n, k, 0)
    
    ans = 0
    for i in range(k):
        spfa()
        ans += d[T]
    
    print(ans)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

problem_description.description: The leader of some very secretive organization has decided to invite all other members to a meeting. All members of the organization live in the same town which can be represented as $$$n$$$ crossroads connected by $$$m$$$ two-directional streets. The meeting will be held in the leader's house near the crossroad $$$1$$$. There are $$$k$$$ members of the organization invited to the meeting; $$$i$$$-th of them lives near the crossroad $$$a_i$$$. All members of the organization receive the message about the meeting at the same moment and start moving to the location where the meeting is held. In the beginning of each minute each person is located at some crossroad. He or she can either wait a minute at this crossroad, or spend a minute to walk from the current crossroad along some street to another crossroad (obviously, it is possible to start walking along the street only if it begins or ends at the current crossroad). In the beginning of the first minute each person is at the crossroad where he or she lives. As soon as a person reaches the crossroad number $$$1$$$, he or she immediately comes to the leader's house and attends the meeting.Obviously, the leader wants all other members of the organization to come up as early as possible. But, since the organization is very secretive, the leader does not want to attract much attention. Let's denote the discontent of the leader as follows  initially the discontent is $$$0$$$;  whenever a person reaches the crossroad number $$$1$$$, the discontent of the leader increases by $$$c \cdot x$$$, where $$$c$$$ is some fixed constant, and $$$x$$$ is the number of minutes it took the person to reach the crossroad number $$$1$$$;  whenever $$$x$$$ members of the organization walk along the same street at the same moment in the same direction, $$$dx^2$$$ is added to the discontent, where $$$d$$$ is some fixed constant. This is not cumulative: for example, if two persons are walking along the same street in the same direction at the same moment, then $$$4d$$$ is added to the discontent, not $$$5d$$$. Before sending a message about the meeting, the leader can tell each member of the organization which path they should choose and where they should wait. Help the leader to establish a plan for every member of the organization so they all reach the crossroad $$$1$$$, and the discontent is minimized.
problem_description.input_spec: The first line of the input contains five integer numbers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$, $$$k$$$, $$$c$$$ and $$$d$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 50$$$, $$$n - 1 \le m \le 50$$$, $$$1 \le k, c, d \le 50$$$) — the number of crossroads, the number of streets, the number of persons invited to the meeting and the constants affecting the discontent, respectively. The second line contains $$$k$$$ numbers $$$a_1$$$, $$$a_2$$$, ..., $$$a_k$$$ ($$$2 \le a_i \le n$$$) — the crossroads where the members of the organization live. Then $$$m$$$ lines follow, each denoting a bidirectional street. Each line contains two integers $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$ ($$$1 \le x_i, y_i \le n$$$, $$$x_i \ne y_i$$$) denoting a street connecting crossroads $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$. There may be multiple streets connecting the same pair of crossroads. It is guaranteed that every crossroad can be reached from every other crossroad using the given streets.
problem_description.output_spec: Print one integer: the minimum discontent of the leader after everyone reaches crossroad $$$1$$$.
problem_description.notes: NoteThe best course of action in the first test is the following:  the first person goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the second person waits one minute on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the third person waits two minutes on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the fourth person waits three minutes on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting.

        self.cap = c
        self.flow = fl
        self.cost = co

graph = [[] for _ in range(1000007)]

parent = [-1] * 1000007
edgeIdx = [-1] * 1000007
inq = [False] * 1000007

S = 1000005
T = 1000006
total = 0

def residual(i):
    return edges[i].cap - edges[i].flow

def spfa():
    global d, parent, edgeIdx, inq
    d = [INF] * 1000007
    parent = [-1] * 1000007
    edgeIdx = [-1] * 1000007
    inq = [False] * 1000007
    
    d[S] = 0
    q = deque()
    q.append(S)
    inq[S] = True
    
    while q:
        u = q.popleft()
        inq[u] = False
        
        for i in graph[u]:
            if not residual(i):
                continue
            v = edges[i].from_node
            w = edges[i].cost
            if d[v] > d[u] + w:
                d[v] = d[u] + w
                parent[v] = u
                edgeIdx[v] = i
                if not inq[v]:

                    q.append(v)

    global total

    graph[u].append(len(edges))
    edges.append(Edge(u, v, cap, 0, cost))
    graph[v].append(len(edges))
    edges.append(Edge(v, u, 0, 0, -cost))

    for t in range(LAYERS):

        v = int(input_line[1]) - 1
        for t in range(LAYERS - 1):

        for t in range(LAYERS - 1):
            for j in range(k):

def process():
    for t in range(LAYERS - 1):
        for i in range(n):
            link(i + t * n, i + (t + 1) * n, k, 0)
    
    for i in range(k):
        augment()
    
    print(total)

def main():
    construct()
    process()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

problem_description.description: The leader of some very secretive organization has decided to invite all other members to a meeting. All members of the organization live in the same town which can be represented as $$$n$$$ crossroads connected by $$$m$$$ two-directional streets. The meeting will be held in the leader's house near the crossroad $$$1$$$. There are $$$k$$$ members of the organization invited to the meeting; $$$i$$$-th of them lives near the crossroad $$$a_i$$$. All members of the organization receive the message about the meeting at the same moment and start moving to the location where the meeting is held. In the beginning of each minute each person is located at some crossroad. He or she can either wait a minute at this crossroad, or spend a minute to walk from the current crossroad along some street to another crossroad (obviously, it is possible to start walking along the street only if it begins or ends at the current crossroad). In the beginning of the first minute each person is at the crossroad where he or she lives. As soon as a person reaches the crossroad number $$$1$$$, he or she immediately comes to the leader's house and attends the meeting.Obviously, the leader wants all other members of the organization to come up as early as possible. But, since the organization is very secretive, the leader does not want to attract much attention. Let's denote the discontent of the leader as follows  initially the discontent is $$$0$$$;  whenever a person reaches the crossroad number $$$1$$$, the discontent of the leader increases by $$$c \cdot x$$$, where $$$c$$$ is some fixed constant, and $$$x$$$ is the number of minutes it took the person to reach the crossroad number $$$1$$$;  whenever $$$x$$$ members of the organization walk along the same street at the same moment in the same direction, $$$dx^2$$$ is added to the discontent, where $$$d$$$ is some fixed constant. This is not cumulative: for example, if two persons are walking along the same street in the same direction at the same moment, then $$$4d$$$ is added to the discontent, not $$$5d$$$. Before sending a message about the meeting, the leader can tell each member of the organization which path they should choose and where they should wait. Help the leader to establish a plan for every member of the organization so they all reach the crossroad $$$1$$$, and the discontent is minimized.
problem_description.input_spec: The first line of the input contains five integer numbers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$, $$$k$$$, $$$c$$$ and $$$d$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 50$$$, $$$n - 1 \le m \le 50$$$, $$$1 \le k, c, d \le 50$$$) — the number of crossroads, the number of streets, the number of persons invited to the meeting and the constants affecting the discontent, respectively. The second line contains $$$k$$$ numbers $$$a_1$$$, $$$a_2$$$, ..., $$$a_k$$$ ($$$2 \le a_i \le n$$$) — the crossroads where the members of the organization live. Then $$$m$$$ lines follow, each denoting a bidirectional street. Each line contains two integers $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$ ($$$1 \le x_i, y_i \le n$$$, $$$x_i \ne y_i$$$) denoting a street connecting crossroads $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$. There may be multiple streets connecting the same pair of crossroads. It is guaranteed that every crossroad can be reached from every other crossroad using the given streets.
problem_description.output_spec: Print one integer: the minimum discontent of the leader after everyone reaches crossroad $$$1$$$.
problem_description.notes: NoteThe best course of action in the first test is the following:  the first person goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the second person waits one minute on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the third person waits two minutes on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the fourth person waits three minutes on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting.

problem_description.description: The leader of some very secretive organization has decided to invite all other members to a meeting. All members of the organization live in the same town which can be represented as $$$n$$$ crossroads connected by $$$m$$$ two-directional streets. The meeting will be held in the leader's house near the crossroad $$$1$$$. There are $$$k$$$ members of the organization invited to the meeting; $$$i$$$-th of them lives near the crossroad $$$a_i$$$. All members of the organization receive the message about the meeting at the same moment and start moving to the location where the meeting is held. In the beginning of each minute each person is located at some crossroad. He or she can either wait a minute at this crossroad, or spend a minute to walk from the current crossroad along some street to another crossroad (obviously, it is possible to start walking along the street only if it begins or ends at the current crossroad). In the beginning of the first minute each person is at the crossroad where he or she lives. As soon as a person reaches the crossroad number $$$1$$$, he or she immediately comes to the leader's house and attends the meeting.Obviously, the leader wants all other members of the organization to come up as early as possible. But, since the organization is very secretive, the leader does not want to attract much attention. Let's denote the discontent of the leader as follows  initially the discontent is $$$0$$$;  whenever a person reaches the crossroad number $$$1$$$, the discontent of the leader increases by $$$c \cdot x$$$, where $$$c$$$ is some fixed constant, and $$$x$$$ is the number of minutes it took the person to reach the crossroad number $$$1$$$;  whenever $$$x$$$ members of the organization walk along the same street at the same moment in the same direction, $$$dx^2$$$ is added to the discontent, where $$$d$$$ is some fixed constant. This is not cumulative: for example, if two persons are walking along the same street in the same direction at the same moment, then $$$4d$$$ is added to the discontent, not $$$5d$$$. Before sending a message about the meeting, the leader can tell each member of the organization which path they should choose and where they should wait. Help the leader to establish a plan for every member of the organization so they all reach the crossroad $$$1$$$, and the discontent is minimized.
problem_description.input_spec: The first line of the input contains five integer numbers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$, $$$k$$$, $$$c$$$ and $$$d$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 50$$$, $$$n - 1 \le m \le 50$$$, $$$1 \le k, c, d \le 50$$$) — the number of crossroads, the number of streets, the number of persons invited to the meeting and the constants affecting the discontent, respectively. The second line contains $$$k$$$ numbers $$$a_1$$$, $$$a_2$$$, ..., $$$a_k$$$ ($$$2 \le a_i \le n$$$) — the crossroads where the members of the organization live. Then $$$m$$$ lines follow, each denoting a bidirectional street. Each line contains two integers $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$ ($$$1 \le x_i, y_i \le n$$$, $$$x_i \ne y_i$$$) denoting a street connecting crossroads $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$. There may be multiple streets connecting the same pair of crossroads. It is guaranteed that every crossroad can be reached from every other crossroad using the given streets.
problem_description.output_spec: Print one integer: the minimum discontent of the leader after everyone reaches crossroad $$$1$$$.
problem_description.notes: NoteThe best course of action in the first test is the following:  the first person goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the second person waits one minute on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the third person waits two minutes on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the fourth person waits three minutes on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting.

problem_description.description: The leader of some very secretive organization has decided to invite all other members to a meeting. All members of the organization live in the same town which can be represented as $$$n$$$ crossroads connected by $$$m$$$ two-directional streets. The meeting will be held in the leader's house near the crossroad $$$1$$$. There are $$$k$$$ members of the organization invited to the meeting; $$$i$$$-th of them lives near the crossroad $$$a_i$$$. All members of the organization receive the message about the meeting at the same moment and start moving to the location where the meeting is held. In the beginning of each minute each person is located at some crossroad. He or she can either wait a minute at this crossroad, or spend a minute to walk from the current crossroad along some street to another crossroad (obviously, it is possible to start walking along the street only if it begins or ends at the current crossroad). In the beginning of the first minute each person is at the crossroad where he or she lives. As soon as a person reaches the crossroad number $$$1$$$, he or she immediately comes to the leader's house and attends the meeting.Obviously, the leader wants all other members of the organization to come up as early as possible. But, since the organization is very secretive, the leader does not want to attract much attention. Let's denote the discontent of the leader as follows  initially the discontent is $$$0$$$;  whenever a person reaches the crossroad number $$$1$$$, the discontent of the leader increases by $$$c \cdot x$$$, where $$$c$$$ is some fixed constant, and $$$x$$$ is the number of minutes it took the person to reach the crossroad number $$$1$$$;  whenever $$$x$$$ members of the organization walk along the same street at the same moment in the same direction, $$$dx^2$$$ is added to the discontent, where $$$d$$$ is some fixed constant. This is not cumulative: for example, if two persons are walking along the same street in the same direction at the same moment, then $$$4d$$$ is added to the discontent, not $$$5d$$$. Before sending a message about the meeting, the leader can tell each member of the organization which path they should choose and where they should wait. Help the leader to establish a plan for every member of the organization so they all reach the crossroad $$$1$$$, and the discontent is minimized.
problem_description.input_spec: The first line of the input contains five integer numbers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$, $$$k$$$, $$$c$$$ and $$$d$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 50$$$, $$$n - 1 \le m \le 50$$$, $$$1 \le k, c, d \le 50$$$) — the number of crossroads, the number of streets, the number of persons invited to the meeting and the constants affecting the discontent, respectively. The second line contains $$$k$$$ numbers $$$a_1$$$, $$$a_2$$$, ..., $$$a_k$$$ ($$$2 \le a_i \le n$$$) — the crossroads where the members of the organization live. Then $$$m$$$ lines follow, each denoting a bidirectional street. Each line contains two integers $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$ ($$$1 \le x_i, y_i \le n$$$, $$$x_i \ne y_i$$$) denoting a street connecting crossroads $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$. There may be multiple streets connecting the same pair of crossroads. It is guaranteed that every crossroad can be reached from every other crossroad using the given streets.
problem_description.output_spec: Print one integer: the minimum discontent of the leader after everyone reaches crossroad $$$1$$$.
problem_description.notes: NoteThe best course of action in the first test is the following:  the first person goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the second person waits one minute on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the third person waits two minutes on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the fourth person waits three minutes on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting.

    def node_id(t, v):
        return t * n + v
    
    # Initialize graph structures
    head = [-1] * MAXN
    prev_idx = [0] * MAXN
    dist = [INF] * MAXN
    inq = [0] * MAXN
    
    # Edge list: each edge is [to, cap, cost, next]
    e = []
    ec = 0
    
    def add_edge(s, d, cap, cost):
        nonlocal ec
        # Forward edge
        e.append([d, cap, cost, head[s]])
        head[s] = ec
        ec += 1
        # Backward edge
        e.append([s, 0, -cost, head[d]])
        head[d] = ec
        ec += 1
    
    # Add edges for starting positions
    S = 0
    T = 6000
    for i in range(1, k + 1):
        add_edge(S, node_id(0, a[i]), 1, 0)
    
    # Add edges for time transitions
    for t in range(0, 101):
        # Move from node i at time t to node i at time t+1 (waiting)
        for i in range(2, n + 1):
            add_edge(node_id(t, i), node_id(t + 1, i), k, c)
        
        # Connect node 1 to sink
        add_edge(node_id(t, 1), T, k, 0)
        
        # Add edges for the m roads
        for i in range(1, m + 1):
            limit = min(k, 25)
            for j in range(1, limit + 1):
                cost = c + (2 * j - 1) * d
                add_edge(node_id(t, u[i]), node_id(t + 1, v[i]), 1, cost)
                add_edge(node_id(t, v[i]), node_id(t + 1, u[i]), 1, cost)
    
    total = 0
    
    def spfa(src, dst):
        nonlocal dist, inq, prev_idx
        dist = [INF] * MAXN
        inq = [0] * MAXN
        q = deque()
        q.append(src)
        dist[src] = 0

            cur = q.popleft()

                    dist[to] = dist[cur] + cost
                    prev_idx[to] = i
                    if inq[to] == 0:

                        inq[to] = 1
                i = nxt

    def update(src, dst):
        nonlocal total
        cur = dst
        while cur != src:
            # Get the edge index
            edge_idx = prev_idx[cur]

            e[edge_idx][1] -= 1
            # Increase capacity of backward edge
            e[edge_idx ^ 1][1] += 1
            # Move to previous node
            cur = e[edge_idx ^ 1][0]
        total += dist[dst]
    
    while spfa(S, T):
        update(S, T)
    
    print(total)

    edges = []
    edge_idx = 0
    
    def encode(t, v):
        return t * n + v
    
    def insert_edge(src, dst, cap, cost):
        nonlocal edge_idx
        edges.append({'target': dst, 'capacity': cap, 'weight': cost, 'next_edge': adj_head[src]})
        adj_head[src] = edge_idx
        edge_idx += 1
        edges.append({'target': src, 'capacity': 0, 'weight': -cost, 'next_edge': adj_head[dst]})
        adj_head[dst] = edge_idx
        edge_idx += 1

        insert_edge(encode(t, 1), sink, k, 0)
        for i in range(1, m + 1):

            for j in range(1, max_j + 1):

                insert_edge(encode(t, froms[i]), encode(t + 1, tos[i]), 1, cost)
                insert_edge(encode(t, tos[i]), encode(t + 1, froms[i]), 1, cost)
    
    shortest_dist = [INF] * MAXN
    in_queue = [0] * MAXN
    prev_edge = [0] * MAXN
    min_cost = 0
    
    def find_min_cost_path(source, sink):
        for i in range(MAXN):
            shortest_dist[i] = INF
        bfs_queue = deque()
        bfs_queue.append(source)
        shortest_dist[source] = 0
        while bfs_queue:

            edges[edge_idx_aug ^ 1]['capacity'] += 1

problem_description.description: The leader of some very secretive organization has decided to invite all other members to a meeting. All members of the organization live in the same town which can be represented as $$$n$$$ crossroads connected by $$$m$$$ two-directional streets. The meeting will be held in the leader's house near the crossroad $$$1$$$. There are $$$k$$$ members of the organization invited to the meeting; $$$i$$$-th of them lives near the crossroad $$$a_i$$$. All members of the organization receive the message about the meeting at the same moment and start moving to the location where the meeting is held. In the beginning of each minute each person is located at some crossroad. He or she can either wait a minute at this crossroad, or spend a minute to walk from the current crossroad along some street to another crossroad (obviously, it is possible to start walking along the street only if it begins or ends at the current crossroad). In the beginning of the first minute each person is at the crossroad where he or she lives. As soon as a person reaches the crossroad number $$$1$$$, he or she immediately comes to the leader's house and attends the meeting.Obviously, the leader wants all other members of the organization to come up as early as possible. But, since the organization is very secretive, the leader does not want to attract much attention. Let's denote the discontent of the leader as follows  initially the discontent is $$$0$$$;  whenever a person reaches the crossroad number $$$1$$$, the discontent of the leader increases by $$$c \cdot x$$$, where $$$c$$$ is some fixed constant, and $$$x$$$ is the number of minutes it took the person to reach the crossroad number $$$1$$$;  whenever $$$x$$$ members of the organization walk along the same street at the same moment in the same direction, $$$dx^2$$$ is added to the discontent, where $$$d$$$ is some fixed constant. This is not cumulative: for example, if two persons are walking along the same street in the same direction at the same moment, then $$$4d$$$ is added to the discontent, not $$$5d$$$. Before sending a message about the meeting, the leader can tell each member of the organization which path they should choose and where they should wait. Help the leader to establish a plan for every member of the organization so they all reach the crossroad $$$1$$$, and the discontent is minimized.
problem_description.input_spec: The first line of the input contains five integer numbers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$, $$$k$$$, $$$c$$$ and $$$d$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 50$$$, $$$n - 1 \le m \le 50$$$, $$$1 \le k, c, d \le 50$$$) — the number of crossroads, the number of streets, the number of persons invited to the meeting and the constants affecting the discontent, respectively. The second line contains $$$k$$$ numbers $$$a_1$$$, $$$a_2$$$, ..., $$$a_k$$$ ($$$2 \le a_i \le n$$$) — the crossroads where the members of the organization live. Then $$$m$$$ lines follow, each denoting a bidirectional street. Each line contains two integers $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$ ($$$1 \le x_i, y_i \le n$$$, $$$x_i \ne y_i$$$) denoting a street connecting crossroads $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$. There may be multiple streets connecting the same pair of crossroads. It is guaranteed that every crossroad can be reached from every other crossroad using the given streets.
problem_description.output_spec: Print one integer: the minimum discontent of the leader after everyone reaches crossroad $$$1$$$.
problem_description.notes: NoteThe best course of action in the first test is the following:  the first person goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the second person waits one minute on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the third person waits two minutes on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the fourth person waits three minutes on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting.

In the social net "TheContact!" for each course of this faculty there is the special group whose name equals the year of university entrance of corresponding course of students at the university. Each of students joins the group of his course and joins all groups for which the year of student's university entrance differs by no more than x from the year of university entrance of this student, where x — some non-negative integer. A value x is not given, but it can be uniquely determined from the available data. Note that students don't join other groups. You are given the list of groups which the student Igor joined. According to this information you need to determine the year of Igor's university entrance.
problem_description.input_spec: The first line contains the positive odd integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 5) — the number of groups which Igor joined.  The next line contains n distinct integers a1, a2, ..., an (2010 ≤ ai ≤ 2100) — years of student's university entrance for each group in which Igor is the member. It is guaranteed that the input data is correct and the answer always exists. Groups are given randomly.
problem_description.output_spec: Print the year of Igor's university entrance.
problem_description.notes: NoteIn the first test the value x = 1. Igor entered the university in 2015. So he joined groups members of which are students who entered the university in 2014, 2015 and 2016.In the second test the value x = 0. Igor entered only the group which corresponds to the year of his university entrance.

import sys

def answer(v):
    print(v)

def solve(a):
    if len(a) == 0:
        answer(0)
        return
    
    min_val = min(a)
    max_val = max(a)
    
    base = min_val
    diff = max_val - min_val
    half_diff = diff // 2
    result = base + half_diff
    
    answer(result)

def main():
    n = int(sys.stdin.readline().strip())
    
    a = []
    for _ in range(n):
        val = int(sys.stdin.readline().strip())
        a.append(val)
    
    solve(a)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

def merge(arr, l, m, r):
    n1 = m - l + 1
    n2 = r - m
    
    # Create temp arrays
    L = arr[l:l + n1]
    R = arr[m + 1:m + 1 + n2]
    
    # Merge the temp arrays back into arr[l..r]
    i = 0  # Initial index of first subarray
    j = 0  # Initial index of second subarray
    k = l  # Initial index of merged subarray
    
    while i < n1 and j < n2:
        if L[i] <= R[j]:
            arr[k] = L[i]
            i += 1
        else:
            arr[k] = R[j]
            j += 1
        k += 1
    
    # Copy the remaining elements of L[], if there are any
    while i < n1:
        arr[k] = L[i]
        i += 1
        k += 1
    
    # Copy the remaining elements of R[], if there are any
    while j < n2:
        arr[k] = R[j]
        j += 1
        k += 1

def merge_sort(arr, l, r):
    if l < r:
        # Same as (l+r)//2, but avoids overflow for large l and h
        m = l + (r - l) // 2
        
        # Sort first and second halves
        merge_sort(arr, l, m)
        merge_sort(arr, m + 1, r)
        
        merge(arr, l, m, r)

def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    a = [0] * (n + 1)  # 1-indexed array
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        a[i] = int(data[i])
    
    # nth_element equivalent: find median (element at position (n-1)/2 in 1-indexed)
    # Convert to 0-indexed: position (n-1)//2 in 0-indexed corresponds to (n-1)//2 + 1 in 1-indexed
    # But we need the element at position 1 + (n-1)//2 in 1-indexed, which is index (n-1)//2 + 1 in 0-indexed
    # Actually, in the C++ code: a+1+(n-1)/2 means the element at position 1+(n-1)/2 (1-indexed)
    # In 0-indexed, that's index (n-1)//2 + 1
    
    # Since Python list is 0-indexed, we need to adjust
    # The C++ code uses a[1+(n-1)/2] which is the element at position 1+(n-1)/2 (1-indexed)
    # In 0-indexed, that's index (n-1)//2 + 1
    
    # Using nth_element equivalent in Python: sort and get the middle element
    # For median: position (n-1)//2 in 0-indexed for 0-indexed array
    # But our array a[1..n] in C++ corresponds to a[1] to a[n]
    # In Python, we can use a[1:n+1] slice
    
    # Actually, let's simplify: the C++ code finds the element that would be at position (n-1)/2 
    # in the sorted array starting from index 1
    # In 0-indexed terms, it's the element at index (n-1)//2 + 1 in the 1-indexed array
    # which corresponds to index (n-1)//2 + 1 in a 0-indexed list if we keep the 0th element unused
    
    # Let's use the same approach: sort the relevant portion
    temp = a[1:n+1]
    temp.sort()
    result = temp[(n-1)//2]  # (n-1)//2 is the 0-indexed position of the median in sorted temp
    
    print(result)

problem_description.output_spec: Print n real numbers, the i-th of them should be equal to the probability that the i-th video will be present in the cache after 10100 queries. def main():

    idx = 0
    
    while idx < len(data):
        n = int(data[idx])
        k = int(data[idx + 1])
        idx += 2
        
        p = []
        for i in range(n):
            p.append(float(data[idx]))
            idx += 1
        
        # Calculate sum for each subset
        sum_arr = [0.0] * (1 << n)
        for i in range(1 << n):
            for j in range(n):
                if i & (1 << j):
                    sum_arr[i] += p[j]
        
        # Count non-negligible probabilities
        cnt = sum(1 for i in range(n) if p[i] > 1e-5)
        
        if cnt <= k:
            result = []
            for i in range(n):
                pp = 1.0 if p[i] > 1e-5 else 0.0
                result.append(str(pp))
            print(" ".join(result))
            continue

        dp = [0.0] * (1 << n)
        dp[0] = 1.0

            for i in range(n):

                    dp[mask | (1 << i)] += dp[mask] * p[i] / sum_arr[rmask]

        for i in range(n):
            result.append(str(ans[i]))
        print(" ".join(result))

    main()

import sys
import math

def main():
    input_data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    idx = 0
    n = int(input_data[idx]); idx += 1
    k = int(input_data[idx]); idx += 1
    
    p = [0.0] * 20
    for i in range(n):
        p[i] = float(input_data[idx]); idx += 1
    
    # Initialize combination table
    c = [[0.0] * 21 for _ in range(21)]
    c[0][0] = 1.0
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        c[i][0] = 1.0
        for j in range(1, i + 1):
            c[i][j] = c[i-1][j-1] + c[i-1][j]
    
    # Precompute cnt and sum for all masks
    max_mask = 1 << n
    cnt = [0] * max_mask
    sum_mask = [0.0] * max_mask
    
    for mask in range(max_mask):
        cnt[mask] = 0
        sum_mask[mask] = 0.0
        for j in range(n):
            if mask & (1 << j):
                cnt[mask] += 1
                sum_mask[mask] += p[j]
    
    # Compute coefficients
    coef = [0.0] * 21
    coef[0] = 1.0
    for i in range(1, k):
        coef[i] = 0.0
    
    for i in range(k - 1, -1, -1):
        coef[i] = 1.0 - coef[i]
        j = 1
        while i - j >= 0:
            coef[i - j] += c[n - 1 - i + j][j] * coef[i]
            j += 1
    
    # Calculate and print answers
    results = []
    for i in range(n):
        ans = 0.0
        if p[i] > 0.005:
            for mask in range(max_mask):
                if mask & (1 << i):
                    continue
                if cnt[mask] >= k:
                    continue
                ans += coef[cnt[mask]] / (1.0 - sum_mask[mask])

#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;

constexpr int MAX_SIZE = 1000007;
constexpr int MOD = 1000000007;

int p, k;
bool seen[MAX_SIZE];
int freq[MAX_SIZE];
vector<int> lengths;

void explore(int start, int mult) {
    int cur = start;
    int len = 1;
    while ((1LL * mult * cur) % p != start) {
        cur = (1LL * mult * cur) % p;
        seen[cur] = true;
        ++len;
    }
    ++freq[len];
}

bool isNotPrime(int n) {
    if (n < 2) return true;
    for (int i = 2; i * i <= n; ++i) {
        if (n % i == 0) return true;
    }
    return false;
}

int main() {
    ios_base::sync_with_stdio(false);
    cin.tie(nullptr);
    
    cin >> p >> k;
    
    if (k == 0) {
        long long res = 1;
        for (int i = 0; i < p - 1; ++i) {
            res = (res * p) % MOD;
        }
        cout << res << '\n';
        return 0;
    }
    
    for (int i = 0; i < p; ++i) {
        if (!seen[i]) {
            explore(i, k);
        }
    }
    
    for (int i = 1; i <= p; ++i) {
        if (freq[i]) lengths.push_back(i);
    }
    
    long long result = 1;
    for (int idx = 0; idx < lengths.size(); ++idx) {
        int L = lengths[idx];
        long long sum = 0;
        for (int j = 0; j < lengths.size() && 1LL * lengths[j] * lengths[j] <= L; ++j) {
            int d = lengths[j];
            if (L % d == 0) {
                int q = L / d;
                sum = (sum + 1LL * d * freq[d]) % MOD;
                if (d != q) {
                    sum = (sum + 1LL * q * freq[q]) % MOD;
                }
            }
        }
        for (int rep = 0; rep < freq[L]; ++rep) {
            result = (result * sum) % MOD;
        }
    }
    
    cout << result << '\n';
    return 0;
}

    long long res = 1;

        base = (base * base) % MOD;
        exp /= 2;
    }

        while (cur != 1) {
            cur = (cur * k) % p;
            ord++;
            if (ord > p) break;
        }
        cout << fast_pow(p, (p - 1) / ord);
    }
    return 0;
}

        power //= 2
    return r

def binpow(a, b, MOD=1000000007):
    res = 1
    a %= MOD
    while b > 0:
        if b & 1:
            res = (res * a) % MOD
        a = (a * a) % MOD
        b >>= 1
    return res

def main():

    p_val = int(data[0])
    k_val = int(data[1])

        return

            chain_len += 1

using namespace std;

using i64 = long long;
using f80 = long double;

constexpr f80 PI = 3.141592654;
constexpr i64 MAX_SIZE = 1000500;
constexpr i64 MODULO = 1000000007;
constexpr i64 MAX_POW2 = 1000000000;

i64 cycle_counts[MAX_SIZE];
i64 visited[MAX_SIZE];
i64 divisor_sums[MAX_SIZE];

i64 find_cycle_length(i64 node, i64 factor, i64 modulus) {
    i64 length = 0;
    while (true) {
        if (visited[node]) break;
        visited[node] = 1;
        node = (node * factor) % modulus;
        ++length;
    }
    return length;
}

i64 fast_exp(i64 base, i64 exponent) {
    if (exponent == 0) return 1;
    i64 half_result = fast_exp(base, exponent / 2);
    if (exponent % 2 == 0) {
        return (half_result * half_result) % MODULO;
    } else {
        return (base * ((half_result * half_result) % MODULO)) % MODULO;
    }
}

int main() {
    ios::sync_with_stdio(false);
    cin.tie(nullptr);

    i64 n, k;
    scanf("%lld %lld", &n, &k);

    if (k == 0) {
        printf("%lld\n", fast_exp(n, n - 1));
        return 0;
    }

    for (i64 i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        if (!visited[i]) {
            i64 len = find_cycle_length(i, k, n);
            cycle_counts[len]++;
        }
    }

    for (i64 d = 1; d <= n; ++d) {
        for (i64 m = d; m <= n; m += d) {
            if (cycle_counts[m]) {
                divisor_sums[m] += cycle_counts[d] * d;
            }
        }
    }

    i64 answer = 1;
    for (i64 d = 1; d <= n; ++d) {
        if (divisor_sums[d]) {
            answer = (answer * fast_exp(divisor_sums[d], cycle_counts[d])) % MODULO;
        }
    }

    printf("%lld\n", answer);

}

import sys
import math
from collections import defaultdict

def fast_pow(a, p, mod=1000000007):
    res = 1
    mask = 1
    pow_part = a % mod
    bits_count = a.bit_length()  # approximate for C++ sizeof(T)*8
    
    for _ in range(bits_count + 1):
        if p & mask:
            res = (res * pow_part) % mod
        mask <<= 1
        pow_part = (pow_part * pow_part) % mod
    
    return res

def solve(ist, ost, multiple_test_mode):
    try:
        line = ist.readline().strip()
        if not line:
            return False
        parts = line.split()
        p = int(parts[0])
        k = int(parts[1])
    except:
        return False

    if multiple_test_mode and not ist:
        return False

    if k == 0:
        ans = fast_pow(p, p - 1)
        ost.write(str(ans) + "\n")
        return multiple_test_mode

    if k == 1:
        ans = fast_pow(p, p)
        ost.write(str(ans) + "\n")
        return multiple_test_mode

    groups = 0
    used = [0] * (p + 1)
    ans = 1

    for x in range(1, p):
        if used[x]:
            continue

        groups += 1
        ans = (ans * p) % 1000000007

        used[x] = 1

        v = x
        while (v * k) % p != 0 and not used[(v * k) % p]:
            used[(v * k) % p] = 1
            v = (v * k) % p

    ost.write(str(ans) + "\n")
    return multiple_test_mode

    input_lines = sys.stdin.read().splitlines()
    input_index = 0
    
    def readline():
        nonlocal input_index
        if input_index < len(input_lines):
            line = input_lines[input_index]
            input_index += 1
            return line
        return ""
    
    ist = type('IStream', (), {'readline': readline})()
    ost = sys.stdout
    
    while solve(ist, ost, True):
        pass

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    if k == 0:
        for i in range(p - 1):
            result = (result * p) % MOD
    else:
        # DSU implementation
        par = list(range(p))
        sz = [1] * p
        comp = p
        
        def find(x):
            if par[x] != x:
                par[x] = find(par[x])
            return par[x]
        
        def unite(x, y):
            nonlocal comp
            x = find(x)
            y = find(y)
            if x == y:
                return False
            if sz[x] > sz[y]:
                x, y = y, x
            # Adjust components based on sizes
            if sz[x] > 1 and sz[y] > 1:
                comp -= 1
            if sz[x] == 1 and sz[y] == 1:
                comp += 1
            par[x] = y
            sz[y] += sz[x]
            return True
        
        for i in range(p):
            j = (k * i) % p
            unite(i, j)
        
        if k > 1:
            components = comp
        else:
            # For k == 1, components = p - number of elements in sz (which is p) = 0?

            # However, for k=1, the unite operations connect everything, so components should be 1

import sys

sys.setrecursionlimit(10000000)

MOD = 1000000007
MAXN = 1000010

p = 0
k = 0
result = 1
visited = [False] * MAXN
cycleLengthCount = [0] * MAXN

def traverse(node, depth):
    global visited, cycleLengthCount
    if visited[node]:
        cycleLengthCount[depth] += 1
        return
    visited[node] = True
    traverse((node * k) % p, depth + 1)

def main():
    global p, k, result, visited, cycleLengthCount
    
    data = input().split()
    p = int(data[0])
    k = int(data[1])
    
    # Reset global variables for each run
    result = 1
    visited = [False] * MAXN
    cycleLengthCount = [0] * MAXN
    
    if k != 0 and k != 1:
        for start in range(1, p):
            if not visited[start]:
                traverse(start, 0)
        
        for length in range(1, p + 1):
            for count in range(cycleLengthCount[length]):
                result = (result * (cycleLengthCount[length] * length + 1)) % MOD
    elif k == 0:
        for i in range(1, p):
            result = (result * p) % MOD
    else:  # k == 1
        for i in range(1, p + 1):
            result = (result * p) % MOD
    
    print(result)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

MOD = 1000000007
maxn = 1000007

def getnum(pos, num_val):
    tep = (num_val * pos) % MOD
    tep = (tep + 1) % MOD
    re = 1
    for _ in range(num_val):
        re = (re * tep) % MOD
    return re

def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    P = int(data[0])
    K = int(data[1])
    
    vis = [0] * maxn
    num = [0] * maxn
    
    if K == 0:
        tepre = 1
        for _ in range(1, P):
            tepre = (tepre * P) % MOD
        print(tepre)
        return
    
    if K == 1:
        tepre = 1
        for _ in range(1, P + 1):
            tepre = (tepre * P) % MOD
        print(tepre)
        return
    
    for i in range(P):
        if vis[i] == 0:
            tepnum = 0
            pos = i
            while vis[pos] == 0:
                vis[pos] = 1
                tepnum += 1
                pos = (K * pos) % P
            num[tepnum] += 1

def modPow(base, exp, MOD=1000000007):
    result = 1
    base %= MOD
    while exp > 0:
        if exp & 1:
            result = (result * base) % MOD
        exp >>= 1
        base = (base * base) % MOD
    return result

def main():
    import sys
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    p = int(data[0])
    k = int(data[1])
    
    if k == 0:
        print(modPow(p, p - 1))
        return
    
    if k == 1:
        print(modPow(p, p))
        return
    
    MAXN = 1000005
    visited = [False] * MAXN
    cycles = 0
    
    for i in range(1, p):
        if visited[i]:
            continue
        current = i
        while not visited[current]:
            visited[current] = True
            current = (current * k) % p
        cycles += 1
    
    print(modPow(p, cycles))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import sys
from collections import deque

def main():
    input = sys.stdin.readline
    MAXN = 202
    INF = 0x3f3f3f3f
    
    # Read input
    line = input().split()
    N = int(line[0])
    T = int(line[1])
    
    initial = []
    target = []
    for _ in range(N):
        initial.append(input().strip())
    for _ in range(N):
        target.append(input().strip())
    
    # Initialize dists with INF
    dists = [[INF] * (N * N) for _ in range(N * N)]
    
    # Find Z position
    Zr, Zc = -1, -1
    for i in range(N):
        for j in range(N):
            if initial[i][j] == 'Z':
                Zr, Zc = i, j
    
    # BFS function
    def bfs_run(r, c, outDists, withCheck):
        Q = deque()
        outDists[r * N + c] = 0
        Q.append((r, c))
        offsets = [(0, 1), (0, -1), (1, 0), (-1, 0)]
        
        while Q:
            x, y = Q.popleft()
            idx = x * N + y
            curDist = outDists[idx]
            
            if withCheck:
                z_idx = Zr * N + Zc
                if dists[z_idx][idx] <= curDist or T <= curDist:
                    if dists[z_idx][idx] < curDist or T < curDist:
                        outDists[idx] = INF + 1
                    continue
            
            for dx, dy in offsets:
                nx, ny = x + dx, y + dy
                if 0 <= nx < N and 0 <= ny < N:
                    if '0' <= target[nx][ny] <= '9':
                        nidx = nx * N + ny
                        if outDists[nidx] == INF:
                            outDists[nidx] = curDist + 1
                            Q.append((nx, ny))
    
    # Run BFS from Z position
    bfs_run(Zr, Zc, dists[Zr * N + Zc], False)
    
    # Run BFS from each digit in initial
    for i in range(N):
        for j in range(N):
            if '1' <= initial[i][j] <= '9':
                bfs_run(i, j, dists[i * N + j], True)
    
    # Setup for max flow
    rowsB = []
    colsB = []
    capacity = [[0] * (2 + N * N + N * N) for _ in range(2 + N * N + N * N)]
    
    # Build graph
    for i in range(N):
        for j in range(N):
            if '1' <= target[i][j] <= '9':
                rowsB.append(i)
                colsB.append(j)
                capacity[(i * N + j) + 2 + N * N][1] = ord(target[i][j]) - ord('0')
    
    zIdx = Zr * N + Zc
    for i in range(N):
        for j in range(N):
            if '1' <= initial[i][j] <= '9':
                idx = i * N + j
                capacity[0][idx + 2] = ord(initial[i][j]) - ord('0')
                for k in range(len(rowsB)):
                    ri = rowsB[k]
                    ci = colsB[k]
                    qi = ri * N + ci
                    if dists[idx][qi] < INF:
                        capacity[idx + 2][qi + 2 + N * N] = INF
    
    # Edmonds-Karp algorithm
    def BFS_edmonds(totalNodes, src, dst):
        flow = [[0] * totalNodes for _ in range(totalNodes)]
        parent = [-1] * totalNodes
        dist = [0] * totalNodes
        queue_bfs = [0] * totalNodes
        
        while True:
            parent = [-1] * totalNodes
            dist[src] = INF
            head = 0
            tail = 0
            queue_bfs[tail] = src
            tail += 1
            
            while head < tail and parent[dst] < 0:
                node = queue_bfs[head]
                head += 1
                for u in range(totalNodes):
                    if parent[u] < 0 and (v := capacity[node][u] - flow[node][u]) > 0:
                        parent[u] = node
                        queue_bfs[tail] = u
                        tail += 1
                        dist[u] = min(dist[node], v)
            
            if parent[dst] < 0:
                break
            
            path_flow = dist[dst]
            u = dst
            while u != src:
                flow[parent[u]][u] += path_flow
                flow[u][parent[u]] -= path_flow
                u = parent[u]
        
        total = 0
        for u in range(totalNodes):
            total += flow[src][u]
        return total
    
    # Calculate and print result
    result = BFS_edmonds(2 + N * N + N * N, 0, 1)
    print(result)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import sys
from collections import deque

SIZE = 202
INF_VAL = 0x3f3f3f3f

flow_flow = [[0] * SIZE for _ in range(SIZE)]
capacity_flow = [[0] * SIZE for _ in range(SIZE)]
prev_node = [0] * SIZE
queue_arr = [0] * SIZE
dist_arr = [0] * SIZE

def max_flow(total_nodes, src, dst):
    while True:
        prev_node = [-1] * total_nodes
        dist_arr[src] = INF_VAL
        f = 0
        r = 0
        queue_arr[r] = src
        r += 1
        while f < r and prev_node[dst] < 0:
            cur = queue_arr[f]
            f += 1
            for node in range(total_nodes):
                if prev_node[node] < 0:
                    res_cap = capacity_flow[cur][node] - flow_flow[cur][node]
                    if res_cap > 0:
                        queue_arr[r] = node
                        r += 1
                        prev_node[node] = cur
                        dist_arr[node] = min(dist_arr[cur], res_cap)
        if prev_node[dst] < 0:
            break
        aug = dist_arr[dst]
        nd = dst
        while nd != src:
            flow_flow[prev_node[nd]][nd] += aug
            flow_flow[nd][prev_node[nd]] -= aug
            nd = prev_node[nd]
    total = 0
    for nd in range(total_nodes):
        total += flow_flow[src][nd]
    return total

board_in = [[''] * 11 for _ in range(11)]
board_out = [[''] * 11 for _ in range(11)]
zombie_i = 0
zombie_j = 0
move_dx = [0, 0, 1, -1]
move_dy = [1, -1, 0, 0]
dist_table = [[0] * 101 for _ in range(101)]
grid_size = 0
time_limit = 0
lst_row = []
lst_col = []

def bfs_compute(si, sj, result_dist, check_flag):
    q = deque()
    result_dist[si * grid_size + sj] = 0
    q.append((si, sj))
    while q:
        i, j = q.popleft()
        idx = i * grid_size + j
        d_val = result_dist[idx]
        if check_flag:
            if dist_table[zombie_i * grid_size + zombie_j][idx] <= d_val or time_limit <= d_val:
                if dist_table[zombie_i * grid_size + zombie_j][idx] < d_val or time_limit < d_val:
                    result_dist[idx] = INF_VAL + 1
                continue
        for k in range(4):
            ni = i + move_dx[k]
            nj = j + move_dy[k]
            if ni < 0 or nj < 0 or ni == grid_size or nj == grid_size:
                continue
            ch = board_out[ni][nj]
            if ch < '0' or ch > '9':
                continue
            nidx = ni * grid_size + nj
            if result_dist[nidx] != INF_VAL:
                continue
            result_dist[nidx] = d_val + 1
            q.append((ni, nj))

def prepare_graph():
    for i in range(grid_size):
        for j in range(grid_size):
            c = board_out[i][j]
            if '1' <= c <= '9':
                lst_row.append(i)
                lst_col.append(j)
                idx = i * grid_size + j
                capacity_flow[idx + 2 + grid_size * grid_size][1] = ord(c) - ord('0')
    z_idx = zombie_i * grid_size + zombie_j
    for i in range(grid_size):
        for j in range(grid_size):
            c = board_in[i][j]
            if '1' <= c <= '9':
                idx = i * grid_size + j
                capacity_flow[0][idx + 2] = ord(c) - ord('0')
                for k in range(len(lst_row)):
                    ri = lst_row[k]
                    ci = lst_col[k]
                    q_idx = ri * grid_size + ci
                    if dist_table[idx][q_idx] < INF_VAL:
                        capacity_flow[idx + 2][q_idx + 2 + grid_size * grid_size] = INF_VAL

def main():
    global grid_size, time_limit, zombie_i, zombie_j
    input_data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    idx = 0
    grid_size = int(input_data[idx])
    idx += 1
    time_limit = int(input_data[idx])
    idx += 1
    
    for i in range(grid_size):
        board_in[i] = list(input_data[idx])
        idx += 1
    
    for i in range(grid_size):
        board_out[i] = list(input_data[idx])
        idx += 1
    
    for i in range(grid_size):
        for j in range(grid_size):
            if board_in[i][j] == 'Z':
                zombie_i = i
                zombie_j = j
    
    # Initialize dist_table with INF_VAL
    for i in range(101):
        for j in range(101):
            dist_table[i][j] = INF_VAL
    
    bfs_compute(zombie_i, zombie_j, dist_table[zombie_i * grid_size + zombie_j], False)
    
    for i in range(grid_size):
        for j in range(grid_size):
            if '1' <= board_in[i][j] <= '9':
                bfs_compute(i, j, dist_table[i * grid_size + j], True)
    
    prepare_graph()
    result = max_flow(2 + grid_size * grid_size + grid_size * grid_size, 0, 1)
    print(result)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import sys
from collections import deque
import heapq

def main():
    input = sys.stdin.read
    data = input().split()
    
    idx = 0
    n = int(data[idx]); idx += 1
    t = int(data[idx]); idx += 1
    
    a = [['' for _ in range(n)] for _ in range(n)]
    b = [['' for _ in range(n)] for _ in range(n)]
    
    br, bc = 0, 0
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(n):
            a[i][j] = data[idx]; idx += 1
            if a[i][j] == 'Z':
                br, bc = i, j
    
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(n):
            b[i][j] = data[idx]; idx += 1
    
    # BFS1: compute bum distances from 'Z'
    Inf = 1000000000
    Maxn = 11
    Maxd = 4
    dy = [-1, 0, 1, 0]
    dx = [0, -1, 0, 1]
    
    bum = [[t] * Maxn for _ in range(Maxn)]
    bum[br][bc] = 0
    Q = deque()
    Q.append((br, bc))
    
    while Q:
        v = Q.popleft()
        d = bum[v[0]][v[1]]
        for i in range(Maxd):
            u = (v[0] + dy[i], v[1] + dx[i])
            if 0 <= u[0] < n and 0 <= u[1] < n and a[u[0]][u[1]] != 'Y' and d + 1 < bum[u[0]][u[1]]:
                bum[u[0]][u[1]] = d + 1
                Q.append(u)
    
    # BFS2: compute dist and pos from a starting point
    def BFS2(sr, sc):
        dist = [[Inf] * Maxn for _ in range(Maxn)]
        pos = [[False] * Maxn for _ in range(Maxn)]
        dist[sr][sc] = 0
        pos[sr][sc] = True
        Q = deque()
        Q.append((sr, sc))
        
        while Q:
            v = Q.popleft()
            d = dist[v[0]][v[1]]
            pos[v[0]][v[1]] = d <= bum[v[0]][v[1]]
            if d >= bum[v[0]][v[1]]:
                continue
            for i in range(Maxd):
                u = (v[0] + dy[i], v[1] + dx[i])
                if 0 <= u[0] < n and 0 <= u[1] < n and a[u[0]][u[1]] != 'Y' and d + 1 < dist[u[0]][u[1]]:
                    dist[u[0]][u[1]] = d + 1
                    Q.append(u)
        return dist, pos
    
    # Build graph for max flow
    N = 2 * n * n + 2
    R = [[0] * N for _ in range(N)]
    neigh = [[] for _ in range(N)]
    
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(n):
            if a[i][j].isdigit() and a[i][j] > '0':
                v = i * n + j + 1
                R[0][v] = ord(a[i][j]) - ord('0')
                neigh[0].append(v)
                neigh[v].append(0)
                
                dist, pos = BFS2(i, j)
                
                for i2 in range(n):
                    for j2 in range(n):
                        if pos[i2][j2] and b[i2][j2].isdigit() and b[i2][j2] > '0':
                            u = n * n + i2 * n + j2 + 1
                            R[v][u] = Inf
                            neigh[v].append(u)
                            neigh[u].append(v)
    
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(n):
            if b[i][j].isdigit() and b[i][j] > '0':
                u = n * n + i * n + j + 1

    P = [0] * N
    res = 0
    
    def getFlow():
        for i in range(N):
            F[i] = 0
        F[0] = Inf
        Q = []
        heapq.heappush(Q, (-Inf, 0))  # Use negative for max-heap behavior
        
        while Q:
            f, v = heapq.heappop(Q)
            f = -f
            if F[v] != f:
                continue
            for u in neigh[v]:
                new_flow = min(f, R[v][u])
                if new_flow > F[u]:
                    F[u] = new_flow
                    P[u] = v
                    heapq.heappush(Q, (-F[u], u))
        
        v = N - 1
        if F[v] == 0:
            return 0
        flow_val = F[v]
        while v:
            u = P[v]
            R[u][v] -= flow_val
            R[v][u] += flow_val
            v = u
        return flow_val
    
    f = getFlow()
    while f != 0:
        res += f
        f = getFlow()
    
    print(res)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

In one nuclear reactor of a research station an uncontrolled reaction is in progress and explosion which will destroy the whole station will happen soon.The station is represented by a square n × n divided into 1 × 1 blocks. Each block is either a reactor or a laboratory. There can be several reactors and exactly one of them will explode soon. The reactors can be considered impassable blocks, but one can move through laboratories. Between any two laboratories, which are in adjacent blocks, there is a corridor. Blocks are considered adjacent if they have a common edge.In each laboratory there is some number of scientists and some number of rescue capsules. Once the scientist climbs into a capsule, he is considered to be saved. Each capsule has room for not more than one scientist.The reactor, which is about to explode, is damaged and a toxic coolant trickles from it into the neighboring blocks. The block, which contains the reactor, is considered infected. Every minute the coolant spreads over the laboratories through corridors. If at some moment one of the blocks is infected, then the next minute all the neighboring laboratories also become infected. Once a lab is infected, all the scientists there that are not in rescue capsules die. The coolant does not spread through reactor blocks.There are exactly t minutes to the explosion. Any scientist in a minute can move down the corridor to the next lab, if it is not infected. On any corridor an unlimited number of scientists can simultaneously move in both directions. It is believed that the scientists inside a lab moves without consuming time. Moreover, any scientist could get into the rescue capsule instantly. It is also believed that any scientist at any given moment always has the time to perform their actions (move from the given laboratory into the next one, or climb into the rescue capsule) before the laboratory will be infected.Find the maximum number of scientists who will be able to escape.
problem_description.input_spec: The first line contains two integers n and t (2 ≤ n ≤ 10, 1 ≤ t ≤ 60). Each of the next n lines contains n characters. These lines describe the scientists' locations. Then exactly one empty line follows. Each of the next n more lines contains n characters. These lines describe the rescue capsules' locations. In the description of the scientists' locations those numbers stand for the number of scientists in the corresponding laboratories. In the rescue capsules' descriptions they stand for the number of such capsules in each laboratory.

MAX_EDGES = 100100
INFINITY_VAL = (1 << 29)

class Edge:
    def __init__(self, destination, flow, capacity, next_edge):
        self.destination = destination
        self.flow = flow
        self.capacity = capacity
        self.next_edge = next_edge

edges = [Edge(0, 0, 0, 0) for _ in range(2 * MAX_EDGES)]
adjacency_head = [0] * MAX_NODES
current_level_ptr = [0] * MAX_NODES
level = [0] * MAX_NODES
bfs_queue = [0] * MAX_NODES
num_edges = 0
total_nodes = 0
src_node = 0
sink_node = 0
queue_tail = 0
queue_head = 0

def reset_flow_network(n_nodes, source, sink):
    global num_edges, total_nodes, src_node, sink_node
    total_nodes = n_nodes
    src_node = source
    sink_node = sink
    num_edges = 2
    for i in range(n_nodes + 1):
        adjacency_head[i] = 0

def connect_nodes(u, v, cap):
    global num_edges
    edges[num_edges] = Edge(v, 0, cap, adjacency_head[u])
    adjacency_head[u] = num_edges
    num_edges += 1
    edges[num_edges] = Edge(u, 0, 0, adjacency_head[v])
    adjacency_head[v] = num_edges
    num_edges += 1

def build_level_graph():
    global queue_tail, queue_head
    for i in range(total_nodes + 1):
        level[i] = 0
    queue_tail = queue_head = 0
    bfs_queue[queue_tail] = src_node
    queue_tail += 1
    level[src_node] = 1
    while queue_head < queue_tail and not level[sink_node]:
        node = bfs_queue[queue_head]
        queue_head += 1
        idx = adjacency_head[node]
        while idx:
            next_node = edges[idx].destination
            if not level[next_node] and edges[idx].flow < edges[idx].capacity:
                level[next_node] = level[node] + 1
                bfs_queue[queue_tail] = next_node
                queue_tail += 1
            idx = edges[idx].next_edge
    return level[sink_node]

def push_flow(node, bottleneck):
    if node == sink_node:
        return bottleneck
    idx = current_level_ptr[node]
    while idx:
        next_node = edges[idx].destination
        if level[node] < level[next_node] and edges[idx].flow < edges[idx].capacity:
            new_bottleneck = min(bottleneck, edges[idx].capacity - edges[idx].flow)
            result = push_flow(next_node, new_bottleneck)
            if result:
                edges[idx].flow += result
                edges[idx ^ 1].flow -= result
                return result
        current_level_ptr[node] = edges[idx].next_edge
        idx = current_level_ptr[node]
    return 0

    total = 0
    while build_level_graph():
        for i in range(total_nodes + 1):
            current_level_ptr[i] = adjacency_head[i]
        delta = push_flow(src_node, INFINITY_VAL)
        while delta:
            total += delta
            delta = push_flow(src_node, INFINITY_VAL)
    return total

import sys
from collections import deque

MAX_BOARD_DIM = 11
MAX_VERTEX_COUNT = 1000
MAX_EDGE_COUNT = 100100
LARGE_VALUE = (1 << 29)

# Graph edge structure simulation using dictionaries
class Edge:
    def __init__(self, dest, cur_flow, cap, next_edge):
        self.dest = dest
        self.cur_flow = cur_flow
        self.cap = cap
        self.next = next_edge

graph_edge = [None] * (2 * MAX_EDGE_COUNT)
first_edge = [0] * MAX_VERTEX_COUNT
ptr_level = [0] * MAX_VERTEX_COUNT
level_arr = [0] * MAX_VERTEX_COUNT
bfs_list = [0] * MAX_VERTEX_COUNT
total_edges = 0
total_nodes = 0
start_node = 0
end_node = 0
queue_end = 0
queue_start = 0

def setup_flow(node_cnt, src, dst):
    global total_nodes, start_node, end_node, total_edges
    total_nodes = node_cnt
    start_node = src
    end_node = dst
    total_edges = 2
    for i in range(total_nodes + 1):
        first_edge[i] = 0

def add_connection(u, v, cap):
    global total_edges
    graph_edge[total_edges] = Edge(v, 0, cap, first_edge[u])
    first_edge[u] = total_edges
    total_edges += 1
    graph_edge[total_edges] = Edge(u, 0, 0, first_edge[v])
    first_edge[v] = total_edges
    total_edges += 1

def create_levels():
    global queue_end, queue_start
    for i in range(total_nodes + 1):
        level_arr[i] = 0
    queue_end = queue_start = 0
    bfs_list[queue_end] = start_node
    queue_end += 1
    level_arr[start_node] = 1
    while queue_start < queue_end and not level_arr[end_node]:
        u = bfs_list[queue_start]
        queue_start += 1
        e = first_edge[u]
        while e:
            v = graph_edge[e].dest
            if not level_arr[v] and graph_edge[e].cur_flow < graph_edge[e].cap:
                level_arr[v] = level_arr[u] + 1
                bfs_list[queue_end] = v
                queue_end += 1
            e = graph_edge[e].next
    return level_arr[end_node]

def augment_path(u, bottleneck):
    if u == end_node:
        return bottleneck
    e = ptr_level[u]
    while e:
        v = graph_edge[e].dest
        if level_arr[u] < level_arr[v] and graph_edge[e].cur_flow < graph_edge[e].cap:
            new_bottleneck = min(bottleneck, graph_edge[e].cap - graph_edge[e].cur_flow)
            flow = augment_path(v, new_bottleneck)
            if flow:
                graph_edge[e].cur_flow += flow
                graph_edge[e ^ 1].cur_flow -= flow
                return flow
        ptr_level[u] = graph_edge[e].next
        e = ptr_level[u]
    return 0

def compute_max_flow():
    result = 0
    while create_levels():
        for i in range(total_nodes + 1):
            ptr_level[i] = first_edge[i]
        delta = augment_path(start_node, LARGE_VALUE)
        while delta:
            result += delta
            delta = augment_path(start_node, LARGE_VALUE)
    return result

size_grid = 0
grid_A = [""] * MAX_BOARD_DIM
grid_B = [""] * MAX_BOARD_DIM

dr = [0, 1, 0, -1]
dc = [1, 0, -1, 0]

def valid_cell(r, c):
    return 0 <= r < size_grid and 0 <= c < size_grid and grid_A[r][c] != 'Y' and grid_A[r][c] != 'Z'

time_stamps = [[[0 for _ in range(MAX_BOARD_DIM)] for _ in range(MAX_BOARD_DIM)] for _ in range(2)]

def expand_bfs(start_r, start_c, idx):
    for r in range(MAX_BOARD_DIM):
        for c in range(MAX_BOARD_DIM):
            time_stamps[idx][r][c] = 0
    time_stamps[idx][start_r][start_c] = 1
    q = deque()
    q.append((start_r, start_c))
    while q:
        r, c = q.popleft()
        if idx == 1 and time_stamps[0][r][c] and time_stamps[0][r][c] <= time_stamps[1][r][c]:
            continue
        for k in range(4):
            nr = r + dr[k]
            nc = c + dc[k]
            if valid_cell(nr, nc) and not time_stamps[idx][nr][nc]:
                time_stamps[idx][nr][nc] = time_stamps[idx][r][c] + 1
                q.append((nr, nc))

node_id = [[[0 for _ in range(MAX_BOARD_DIM)] for _ in range(MAX_BOARD_DIM)] for _ in range(2)]

def main():

                pos_Zr, pos_Zc = r, c

    for r in range(size_grid):

        for c in range(size_grid):
            if grid_B[r][c] != 'Y' and grid_B[r][c] != 'Z':
                total_node_num += 1
                node_id[1][r][c] = total_node_num
    
    total_node_num += 1
    source_v = 0
    sink_v = total_node_num
    setup_flow(total_node_num, source_v, sink_v)
    
    for r in range(size_grid):
        for c in range(size_grid):
            if grid_A[r][c] != 'Z' and grid_A[r][c] != 'Y':
                add_connection(source_v, node_id[0][r][c], ord(grid_A[r][c]) - ord('0'))
                add_connection(node_id[1][r][c], sink_v, ord(grid_B[r][c]) - ord('0'))
    
    expand_bfs(pos_Zr, pos_Zc, 0)
    
    for r in range(size_grid):
        for c in range(size_grid):
            if '0' < grid_A[r][c] <= '9':
                expand_bfs(r, c, 1)
                for rr in range(size_grid):
                    for cc in range(size_grid):
                        if '0' < grid_B[rr][cc] <= '9':
                            if time_stamps[1][rr][cc] and (not time_stamps[0][rr][cc] or time_stamps[0][rr][cc] >= time_stamps[1][rr][cc]) and time_stamps[1][rr][cc] - 1 <= limit_T:
                                add_connection(node_id[0][r][c], node_id[1][rr][cc], LARGE_VALUE)
    
    print(compute_max_flow())
